content.title: [I01] Field Refinement: The Specification Settled by Use
content.body:
## Overview

The prototype is used as the tool agents in this workspace invoke, and what that use reveals changes the specification until it stops changing. Every surprise becomes a ledger entry reducible to a fixture; an accepted finding changes the design first, then the corpus, then the build. The initiative ends when every entry is resolved or explicitly deferred and the design and corpus carry one tagged revision, which is the target the production build names.

## Problem

The behavioural contract has been written and reviewed, and nothing has yet bundled a real instruction set for an agent carrying out the procedure it describes.

- **A specification written before use is a hypothesis.**
  The design states its invariants against constructed examples, and names its own residual items as needing measured fixture and real-skill data before their defaults are revisited ([residual policy](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/blob/d45c7f08f3878e71d9d0a99ae728fc69fc21f174/artifacts/planning/2026-10-17-prosiform-v1/design.md#L532-L537)).

- **A corpus built beside an implementation tests what was implemented.**
  Fixtures accumulate from the work that needed them, so a construct real sources carry but nobody implemented has no fixture and produces no failure.

- **A surprise met mid-task has nowhere to go.**
  The agent is doing something else, so without a recorded place for a finding the cheapest action is a local workaround, and the design keeps its original claim.

- **A fix applied to the build leaves the contract wrong.**
  Correcting a bundling in code without changing the design leaves the design asserting the original behaviour, and the next implementation reads the design.

- **A moving contract cannot be implemented twice.**
  A corpus that changes under refinement gives a second implementation no fixed target and no revision it can be said to satisfy.

## Proposal

- **The prototype is the tool in use.**
  It is invoked from this workspace's skills, so the contract meets real sources and real agents rather than constructed examples.

- **The ledger records every run.**
  A bundling run is recorded with the source identities it bundled and its outcome, so how much the tool was used is a fact the ledger holds rather than an impression.

- **Every surprise becomes a ledger entry.**
  An entry carries its date, the invocation, the source identities, the observed result and the expected one, and a triage state naming whether it changes the design, fills a corpus gap, fixes a build defect, or changes nothing.

- **An entry is reducible to a fixture.**
  A capture tool reduces an entry's sources and invocation to the smallest fixture that still reproduces the observed result, so a finding becomes something that can be re-run.

- **A finding changes the design first.**
  The design is the contract; the corpus follows the design, and the build follows the corpus. Each revision cites the entry that motivated it.

- **An accepted finding becomes a row.**
  Rows are added to the revision epic as findings are accepted, so what remains is visible rather than implied.

- **Deferral is a recorded decision.**
  An entry not resolved before the freeze names what is deferred and why, and stays in the ledger for the stage that takes it.

- **A prerequisite list goes when bundling replaces it.**
  A skill's prerequisite section names whole documents, coarsely but completely. It is removed once a recorded bundling supplies what it named, and anything the bundling failed to supply is a ledger entry rather than a silent loss. In its place the skill's own text names the invocation that bundles them, so an agent is told to bundle rather than left to decide.

- **Each run is measured against what it replaces.**
  A run record carries the bundled output size and the whole-file size of the sources it bundled, so the retrieval cost the proposal measured can be compared with the cost of bundling instead.

- **The freeze is a tag.**
  Design and corpus take one tagged revision, and the production build names that revision as its target.

## Work Breakdown

| Epic | Description | Coverage | Depends on | Done |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [E00](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/21) | Findings Ledger | AC1, AC2, AC9 | | |
| [E01](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/22) | Specification Revision | AC3, AC4, AC8 | | |
| [E02](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/23) | Specification Freeze | AC5, AC6, AC7 | | |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** A surprise met while bundling in real use is recorded with the evidence needed to reproduce it without the original session, as the ledger's entries show.
- [ ] **AC2.** A recorded finding is reducible to a corpus fixture that reproduces it, as the capture tool's reduction tests show.
- [ ] **AC3.** An accepted finding changes the design before the corpus or the build, as the revision history citing that finding shows.
- [ ] **AC4.** What remains unsettled is visible without reading the ledger whole, as the open-finding summary shows.
- [ ] **AC5.** Each ledger entry is resolved or carries a recorded deferral naming what is deferred and why, as the ledger's status summary shows.
- [ ] **AC6.** The design and the corpus carry one tagged revision that a production build can name as its target, as the tag shows.
- [ ] **AC7.** The specification is settled only after the tool has bundled each source in a declared exposure set, as the freeze check shows.
- [ ] **AC8.** A prerequisite section is removed only where a recorded bundling supplies what it named, and any shortfall is a ledger entry, as the removal records show.
- [ ] **AC9.** Each exposure-set source carries a bundled size recorded against the size of the same sources read whole, as the run records show.

## Non-Goals

- It does not implement a production build.
- It does not change the outcomes the bundling contract serves.
- It does not restructure a source document beyond removing a prerequisite section bundling has replaced.
- It does not commit to a date for the freeze.
- It does not accept a finding by working around it in a source document.
- It does not open an issue or a pull request on another project.

## References

- **R1.** **Source.** [v1 design](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/blob/d45c7f08f3878e71d9d0a99ae728fc69fc21f174/artifacts/planning/2026-10-17-prosiform-v1/design.md) — the specification this initiative settles, including the residual items it names as needing measured real-skill data.
- **R2.** [Planning decisions](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/blob/d45c7f08f3878e71d9d0a99ae728fc69fc21f174/artifacts/planning/2026-10-17-prosiform-v1/decisions.md) — why the prototype is used before a production build is committed to, and what marks the specification settled.
- **R3.** [Proposal](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/1) — the scoped problem and the goal clauses these criteria trace to.

content.title: [I00] Prototype Compiler: The Contract Proven in Python
content.body:
## Overview

A Python 3 build of prosiform compiles one or more local Markdown document or section references into one continuous, validated Markdown document, and a language-neutral fixture corpus states what that document must be. The corpus declares each case as a source tree, an invocation and an expected result, so it binds any implementation rather than describing this one. The repository is laid out, its environment pinned and its checks runnable before the first of that work lands. The build installs as the tool agents in this workspace invoke, with a wrapper that delivers a bundle whole or reports a delivery failure. The initiative is complete when the corpus covers every behavioural clause of the design, the Python build passes it, and an agent bundles by invoking the installed tool.

## Problem

Modular Markdown authoring separates the destination a link names from the context an operation needs, and nothing closes that gap except the reading agent.

- **Retrieval is prose the agent must execute.**
  One rule directs the agent to read a linked section and its subsections, stop before the next heading of equal or higher level, read that file's prerequisites first, preserve boundaries in batched reads and recover truncated output: [Linked sections](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/blob/acac85867ca963df00251e4cf00a4db11b14bf24/skills/work-planner/SKILL.md#L71-L72).

- **One request reaches 39 documents.**
  [Plan Mode](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/blob/acac85867ca963df00251e4cf00a4db11b14bf24/skills/work-planner/modes/plan-mode.md#L5-L23) lists 15 prerequisites; the transitive closure of its Markdown links is 39 files and 139 distinct section targets, 318,018 bytes read whole.

- **Section boundaries are decided by the reader.**
  519 Markdown links run between the 38 files of that one skill, 363 of them naming a section rather than a file, so each read also decides where the named section ends.

- **Nothing establishes the context was complete.**
  A prerequisite the agent skipped and one it never needed produce the same result: an operation that proceeds.

- **A behavioural contract with no executable form binds nothing.**
  The design states its invariants in prose. Prose cannot report that an implementation violates one.

## Proposal

- **The corpus is the contract.**
  Each fixture declares a source tree, an invocation and the exact expected bundle, exit status and diagnostics. A runner decides pass or fail from the declaration alone, naming no implementation.

- **Python proves the semantics.**
  Dependency closure, overlap consolidation, destination identity and the post-compilation invariants are parser-independent, so a Python build establishes them at a fraction of the cost of establishing them in the production language.

- **The build grows in layers, and the earliest useful layer ships.**
  A whole-document bundling that works end to end comes first. Section selection, dependency closure, destination identity and the one validation check that proves a candidate carries its sources follow, and the tool installs at that point. Boundary safety, diagnostics, validation scope, the outline a partial selection skipped, directory grouping and the measured budget extend a product agents are already invoking.

- **Coverage depth follows the ship rather than preceding it.**
  Each row before the ship carries the fixture that proves its behaviour, and declares its boundary, failure and adversarial cases as fixtures awaiting the conformance epic. A declared fixture that unexpectedly passes fails the run, so a deferral cannot outlive its reason and the corpus names every gap it carries.

- **Span-level editing is out of scope here.**
  Byte-exact source-preserving edits are specific to the production parser and are proven where that parser lives. This build may reconstruct its output, provided the corpus's preservation fixtures hold.

- **The build ships to be used.**
  It installs with a stable entry point and a wrapper owning the delivery contract, because the specification is refined by what real use reveals and nothing is revealed by a build nobody invokes.

- **The conformance report is the handover.**
  It maps every behavioural clause of the design to the fixtures that exercise it, and lists any clause no fixture covers, so the next implementation inherits a measured contract rather than an assumed one.

## Work Breakdown

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [E00](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/26) | Project Foundation | | | ✓ |
| [E01](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/3) | Corpus Harness | AC8 | | ✓ |
| [E02](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/4) | Walking Skeleton | AC7, AC13 | | ✓ |
| [E03](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/5) | Outline Hierarchy | AC5 | | ✓ |
| [E04](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/6) | Dependency Closure | AC1, AC3, AC10 | | ✓ |
| [E05](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/7) | Destination Identity | AC2 | | |
| [E06](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/8) | Candidate Validation | AC4, AC6 | [E05](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/7) | |
| [E07](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/19) | Field Deployment | AC11, AC12 | | |
| [E08](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/59) | Validation Gate | AC6 | [E05](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/7) | |
| [E09](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/60) | Outline and Closure Completion | AC5, AC14 | | |
| [E10](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/9) | Corpus Conformance | AC9 | [E06](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/8) | |
| [E11](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/39) | Deferred Debt | AC15 | | |

The order these epics start in is carried by each one's priority label rather than by this table. A cell here names a prerequisite only where every task of the dependent epic requires every task of the one named; every other edge stays in the task tables, so an epic starts on the rows that are free and waits only on the rows that are not.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **AC1.** A bundling returns one Markdown document holding the selected content and every local Markdown dependency reachable from it, as the corpus runner's output comparison shows.
- [ ] **AC2.** Each internal reference in a published bundle resolves to exactly one destination within that bundle, as the corpus runner's destination check shows.
- [x] **AC3.** Each selected source region appears once in a published bundle however many reference paths reach it, as the corpus runner's output comparison shows.
- [ ] **AC4.** Selected instruction wording and code examples are byte-identical to their sources apart from the transformations the declared profile names, as the corpus runner's preservation check shows.
- [ ] **AC5.** Each selected section keeps its ancestor chain and its relative depth beneath the heading naming its source file, as the corpus runner's outline comparison shows.
- [ ] **AC6.** A bundling that fails validation publishes nothing, exits nonzero and writes a diagnostic carrying the defect, its source location, the offending reference and the inclusion chain, as the corpus's failure fixtures show.
- [x] **AC7.** A document bundles with no markup beyond ordinary Markdown links and headings, as the fixtures taken from unmodified workspace skills show.
- [x] **AC8.** A fixture declares its sources, its invocation and its expected result, and the runner decides pass or fail from that declaration alone, as the runner's own test suite shows.
- [ ] **AC9.** Every behavioural clause the design states maps to at least one corpus fixture, or is listed as uncovered, as the conformance report shows.
- [x] **AC10.** Each resource limit the profile names fails at the first boundary it crosses, publishing nothing, as the corpus's limit fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC11.** An agent bundles its context by invoking the installed tool rather than by reading the linked documents itself, as the installation smoke run against a documented entry point shows.
- [ ] **AC12.** A bundle the transport cannot deliver whole is reported as a delivery failure rather than as a truncated success, as the corpus's delivery fixtures show.
- [x] **AC13.** A corpus run reproduces on a fresh checkout at the dependency versions a lockfile records, as the continuous-integration run shows.
- [ ] **AC14.** The output budget rests on the measured size of a real bundling rather than an assumed figure, as the recorded measurement shows.
- [ ] **AC15.** The technical debt this initiative's delivery defers is fixed, as the Done column of its final epic's Work Breakdown shows.

## Non-Goals

- It does not apply byte-exact edits to identified source spans.
- It does not create the production build's tree, toolchain or dependencies.
- It does not settle the specification, which use refines.
- It does not execute, authorize or sequence the procedures it bundles.
- It does not infer a dependency the source did not state as a Markdown link.
- It does not fetch remote documents, resources or URLs.
- It does not accept its own output as a source document.

## References

- **R1.** **Source.** [v1 design](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/blob/d45c7f08f3878e71d9d0a99ae728fc69fc21f174/artifacts/planning/2026-10-17-prosiform-v1/design.md) — the behavioural contract these criteria answer to: input and output, Markdown profile, section extraction, destination identity, validation invariants and resource limits.
- **R2.** [Planning decisions](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/blob/d45c7f08f3878e71d9d0a99ae728fc69fc21f174/artifacts/planning/2026-10-17-prosiform-v1/decisions.md) — why the prototype is a retained oracle, where the corpus lives, and the measured evidence behind the Problem.
- **R3.** [Proposal](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/1) — the scoped problem and the goal clauses these criteria trace to.

content.title: [I00:E01] Corpus Harness: Fixture Format and the Runner That Executes It
content.body:
## Overview

The corpus harness is the instrument every later criterion in this initiative names. It defines how one fixture declares its sources, its invocation and its expected result, and it supplies the runner that decides pass or fail from that declaration alone. It exists first because a contract that cannot be executed cannot be violated visibly.

## Problem

The behavioural contract exists only as prose, and prose reports nothing when an implementation departs from it.

- **A clause cannot fail.**
  The design states invariants about bundled output, failure behaviour and limits. None of them produces a signal when the output is wrong.

- **A test written against one build binds only that build.**
  Checks expressed in a language's test framework carry that language's assumptions, so a second implementation inherits assertions rather than a contract.

- **A bundling failure has several observable parts.**
  Standard output, exit status and the diagnostic stream each carry part of the result, so a check reading only one of them passes a bundling that failed in the others.

## Proposal

- **A fixture is a directory with a manifest.**
  The directory holds the source tree the fixture bundles. The manifest names the invocation, the expected standard output, the expected exit status and the expected diagnostics, including their error codes. The catalogue of those codes is declared with the schema.

- **The manifest is the whole declaration.**
  The runner reads the manifest and the fixture's files, runs the declared invocation against a build identified by configuration, and compares every declared expectation. It holds no knowledge of any implementation.

- **The failure names belong to the schema.**
  The error codes the design declares are part of the manifest schema, so a fixture expecting a failure names one of them and a manifest naming anything else is rejected as malformed.

- **A failure names the differing region.**
  A mismatch reports which expectation differed and where, so a corpus failure identifies the defect rather than reporting only that a comparison failed.

- **Continuous integration runs the whole corpus.**
  Every change runs every fixture, so a regression surfaces on the change that caused it.

## Work Breakdown

| Task | Description | Coverage | Depends on | Joins | Done |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [W01](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/40) | Fixture layout and manifest schema | AC1, AC5 | [E00:W03](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/26) | | ✓ |
| [W02](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/43) | Corpus runner and result comparison | AC2, AC3 | W01 | | ✓ |
| [W04](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/44) | Documentation held to the project it describes | AC6 | W01 | | ✓ |
| [W05](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/45) | Warning diagnostics, and every document the link check reads | AC7, AC8 | W01 | | ✓ |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **AC1.** A fixture declares its source tree, its invocation, its expected standard output, its expected exit status and its expected diagnostics in one manifest, as the schema validation test shows.
- [x] **AC2.** The runner decides a fixture's result from its manifest and files alone, naming no implementation module or language, as the runner's unit tests show.
- [x] **AC3.** A mismatched expectation is reported with the expectation that differed and the differing region, as the runner's failure tests show.
- [x] **AC5.** A manifest naming an error code outside the declared catalogue fails schema validation, as the schema tests show.
- [x] **AC6.** The build README's dependency and command tables name what the project declares and nothing it does not, as the README check shows.
- [x] **AC7.** A fixture declares the warnings its run emits, and a manifest naming a warning code outside the declared catalogue fails schema validation, as the schema tests show.
- [x] **AC8.** Every reference in every document the repository owns resolves, the fixture corpus excepted, as the link check shows.

## References

content.title: [I00:E02] Walking Skeleton: One Document Bundled, Validated and Published
content.body:
## Overview

The walking skeleton is the smallest prosiform that works end to end: a command that takes a source root and a whole-document reference, reads and parses the document under the declared profile, strips its transport metadata, and publishes one bundle under a heading naming the source file. It carries no dependency traversal and no link rewriting, so the epics after it extend a product that already runs.

## Problem

Nothing executable exists, so every later behaviour has nowhere to attach.

- **The declared profile is a list of options, not a configuration.**
  CommonMark with pipe tables, strikethrough and preserved task markers, with typographic substitution disabled, is stated as a requirement and configured nowhere.

- **Transport metadata reaches bundled content.**
  A leading byte-order mark and leading frontmatter are source transport, not instructions, and would otherwise be published as body text.

- **Success and failure share one stream.**
  Without a declared split, a bundle and the diagnostics explaining a failure arrive together, and a consumer cannot tell a published document from an error report.

- **An exit status carries the only reliable signal.**
  A caller that reads the presence of Markdown as success accepts a truncated or failed run as a complete one.

## Proposal

- **One command, two streams.**
  Bundled Markdown goes to standard output and diagnostics to standard error. Success output holds the bundle and nothing else.

- **The profile is configured explicitly.**
  `markdown-it-py` is configured to the declared profile rather than inheriting a default or an everything-enabled preset, and the configuration is pinned with the profile identifier.

- **Raw HTML is refused, not copied.**
  The bundle carries Markdown and nothing else, so a source with raw HTML in selected content fails rather than passing elements and identifiers the tool neither created nor tracks into the output.

- **An unsupported construct fails rather than becoming prose.**
  Footnotes, wiki links, heading-attribute syntax and transclusion directives are outside the profile. One recognized as a dependency or a section-naming construct in selected content fails the run, because publishing it as literal text would drop a dependency without reporting it. Ordinary prose that merely resembles an extension is left alone.

- **Source encoding is required, not assumed.**
  A source must be valid UTF-8. One that is not fails, rather than being decoded with replacements that change the bytes the tool promises to preserve.

- **Transport metadata is removed by delimiter scanning.**
  One optional leading byte-order mark, then an exactly matching frontmatter opener and closer, are stripped without parsing the metadata. Original source coordinates survive for diagnostics.

- **Each source becomes a file group.**
  Its content is published beneath one generated heading carrying its normalized root-relative path, Markdown extension removed, as escaped literal text, and its own headings move down one level.

- **Real skill documents are fixtures.**
  Documents taken unmodified from this workspace's skills are corpus inputs, so the claim that ordinary Markdown bundles is tested against ordinary Markdown.

## Work Breakdown

| [W02](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/48) | Profile configuration and source parsing | AC5, AC7, AC9 | W01 | | ✓ |
| [W03](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/50) | Byte-order mark and frontmatter removal | AC2, AC8 | W02 | | ✓ |
| [W04](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/53) | Whole-document emission under a filename heading | AC1 | W03 | | ✓ |
| [W05](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/54) | Fixtures from unmodified workspace skills | AC6 | W04 | | ✓ |

| [W07](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/51) | An error code for every failing outcome the contract names | AC12 | W01 | | ✓ |
| [W08](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/58) | Check fixtures for a validation-only run | AC10 | W06 | | ✓ |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **AC1.** A whole-document reference produces one bundle whose source headings sit beneath a generated heading carrying the document's normalized root-relative path without its Markdown extension, as literal text, as the skeleton fixtures show.
- [x] **AC2.** One leading byte-order mark and one leading frontmatter block are absent from bundled content while the body that follows them is unchanged, as the frontmatter fixtures show.
- [x] **AC3.** A successful run writes the bundle to standard output and nothing else to that stream, as the stream fixtures show.
- [x] **AC4.** Each exit status the corpus can express is returned for the outcome the design names, as the exit-status fixtures show, and each status no manifest can declare is returned as the build's own tests show.
- [x] **AC5.** Typographic substitution is absent and source task-list markers survive bundling, as the profile fixtures show.
- [x] **AC6.** A document taken unmodified from a workspace skill bundles with no added markup, as the real-source fixtures show.

- [x] **AC9.** Raw HTML in selected content fails rather than being copied into the bundle, as the HTML fixtures show.
- [x] **AC10.** A validation-only run bundles and validates its entry references and publishes nothing, to either stream or to a named output file, as the check fixtures show.
- [x] **AC11.** Every fixture in the corpus runs against the build on each change, and a build the job cannot reach fails it, as the continuous-integration run shows.
- [x] **AC12.** Each failing outcome the contract names carries a stable error code its catalogue holds, so a fixture can declare that outcome, as the catalogue test and the usage-failure fixtures show.

content.title: [I00:E03] Outline Hierarchy: Sections, the Plus-One Shift and File Groups
content.body:
## Overview

Outline hierarchy makes a partial selection readable. A fragment selects one eligible section and its subsections, every emitted source heading moves down one level beneath its file heading unless that heading already carries the document's own title, and a file group emits what it selected in the order its source wrote it. A selection that skipped most of a document still reads as part of that document.

## Problem

A section lifted out of its document loses the structure that gave it meaning.

- **A fragment names a heading, not a region.**
  Where the named section ends is a decision, and a heading inside a list or a blockquote looks like a terminator without being one.

- **Two heading syntaxes carry one meaning.**
  A Setext heading cannot be shifted by editing a prefix, so a uniform level shift has to convert it while keeping its visible text and inline semantics.

- **A file heading and a document title say the same thing twice.**
  A document opening with its own title, bundled beneath a heading naming its path, carries that name twice and pushes every heading below it one level deeper than it needs.

- **A fragment is renderer-defined.**
  The fragment that reaches a heading is the one the renderer generates from its visible text, including its duplicate numbering, so a lookup that invents its own spelling resolves to the wrong heading or to none.

## Proposal

- **Only document-level headings are selectable roots.**
  A section runs to the next document-level heading of equal or higher level. A heading inside a container does not terminate it, and a fragment naming one fails as an unsupported target.

- **A file group keeps its source order.**
  Selected regions are emitted in the order they appear in their source, so a document's preamble sits after its filename heading and before its first retained heading, and its sections follow one another as written.

- **Headings shift by one, and a duplicated title is absorbed.**
  Every emitted source heading in a file group, inside retained containers included, moves down exactly one level. Where the source's only H1 slugifies to the final segment of its file heading, that heading is not emitted and the group keeps its source levels instead, because the file heading already names it. Relative depth and visible text are preserved, and a Setext heading becomes the equivalent ATX heading.

- **Source fragments come from a compatibility-tested slugger.**
  Visible heading text is derived from the event stream, and the fragment it produces is checked against fixtures covering punctuation, markup, Unicode, duplicates and collisions with naturally suffixed headings.

- **Structure beyond a single group is completed later.**
  Heading-only ancestors, the depth ceiling and directory grouping extend this epic's product rather than condition it, and are delivered by [E09](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/60) once the tool is in use.

## Work Breakdown

| Task | Description | Coverage | Depends on | Joins | Done |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [W01](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/64) | Source heading slugs and the heading index | AC5 | [E02:W02](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/4) | | ✓ |
| [W02](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/72) | Eligible section extraction and boundaries | AC1, AC2 | W01 | | ✓ |
| [W03](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/74) | Plus-one heading shift and Setext conversion | AC1, AC3, AC4 | W02, [E02:W04](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/4) | | ✓ |
| [W04](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/76) | File group emission: absorbed title and source order | AC6, AC7 | W03 | | ✓ |

## Acceptance Criteria

content.title: [I00:E04] Dependency Closure: Recursive Resolution, Consolidation and Budgets
content.body:
## Overview

Dependency closure is what makes a bundle complete. Supported local Markdown links in selected content are resolved, bundled and included; traversal continues until no new content is reachable; overlapping selections become one region; and every budget the profile names fails at its first crossed boundary rather than truncating. This is the epic that turns a document transformer into a compiler.

## Problem

A link identifies a destination and retrieves nothing, and a traversal that is not bounded or consolidated produces the wrong document.

- **A reference graph has cycles.**
  Documents in an instruction set link back to one another, so a traversal without a fixed point repeats regions or does not terminate.

- **The same region arrives by several paths.**
  A section selected directly and again inside a later whole-document inclusion is one region, and emitting it twice makes the bundle disagree with its sources.

- **A link string is not a path.**
  Percent escapes, an encoded delimiter, a query, a relative segment and a symbolic link each change which file a reference names, and a check performed on the string alone can confine a reference that escapes the root.

- **A self-link and an ancestor link look alike.**
  A section linking to itself is a defect, while a nested section linking back to an including ancestor is ordinary, and both are a link whose target is already present.

- **An unbounded compilation fails late or not at all.**
  Without declared budgets, a pathological source tree is discovered by exhausting memory rather than by a diagnostic.

## Proposal

- **References normalize before they resolve.**
  URI components split before percent-decoding, escapes validate strictly, decoding happens exactly once, and `.` and `..` normalize against the proper base. A query on a local Markdown reference, an unsupported scheme and an unsupported path form each fail.

- **The root is enforced by access, not by string inspection.**
  Rooted, no-follow access confines every source read, and a path reaching a source through a symbolic link below the root fails.

- **A bundle does not depend on how it was asked for.**
  File groups are emitted in root-relative path order. Neither discovery order nor argument order decides the arrangement, so the same selection always produces the same bytes. Source order within a file is preserved.

- **Only a Markdown link is a dependency.**
  An image, a script, a stylesheet or any other non-Markdown resource is classified and preserved, never opened and never traversed. Following one would widen every closure that mentions a diagram, and the bundle guarantees Markdown dependencies rather than offline resources.

- **Traversal runs to a fixed point.**
  Newly included content is traversed before compilation completes, so a dependency discovered inside a late inclusion is resolved rather than left out.

- **A reference expands a structural ancestor into its content.**
  A link whose target is present only as a heading-only ancestor expands closure to include that section's selected body, replacing the structural ancestor. A displayed title does not satisfy a reference.

- **Expansion reaches only so far.**
  A target beyond the declared expansion depth, counted in link hops along its shortest path from an entry reference, fails the run. The budget constrains the shape of the reference graph; the file, byte and target budgets bound its size.

- **Overlaps consolidate upward.**
  A later reference including an ancestor section or a whole document replaces the narrower selections inside it, and the larger region's own dependencies are traversed.

- **Identity decides self-reference.**
  A link is compared after canonical path and fragment resolution. A link from a section to that same canonical section fails; a link from a section to an including ancestor resolves to the existing destination. Link ownership is stored separately from inclusion, so consolidation does not change the classification.

- **Budgets fail at the boundary.**
  Each declared limit is counted as the design states and fails the compilation when crossed. No output is truncated to fit. The output budget's figure is settled against a measured bundling by [E09](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/60), which also carries the example tree the design's usage examples name.

## Work Breakdown

| [W02](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/71) | Root confinement and no-symlink source access | AC5 | W01 | | ✓ |
| [W03](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/77) | Link classification and traversal to a fixed point | AC1, AC2, AC12, AC15, AC16 | W02, [E03:W02](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/5) | | ✓ |
| [W04](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/81) | Selection consolidation and expanded coverage | AC3, AC9 | W03 | | ✓ |
| [W05](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/82) | Self-reference, ancestor-reference and marked-resource classification | AC4, AC13, AC17 | W04 | W06 | ✓ |
| [W06](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/82) | Resource budgets fail at the boundary | AC7, AC11 | W04 | W05 | ✓ |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **AC1.** A marked local Markdown link in selected content is resolved, bundled and present in the published bundle, as the traversal fixtures show.
- [x] **AC2.** A cyclic reference graph bundles to a fixed point with each reachable region present once, as the cycle fixtures show.
- [x] **AC3.** A selection contained within a larger selection is represented by the larger region alone, and that region's own references are resolved, as the consolidation fixtures show.
- [x] **AC4.** A link to the same canonical section fails as a direct self-reference, while a link back to an including ancestor resolves to that ancestor's existing destination, as the self-reference fixtures show.
- [x] **AC5.** A reference whose normalized path leaves the allowed root, or reaches a source through a symbolic link below it, fails with its declared error code, as the confinement fixtures show.
- [x] **AC6.** A schemeless reference carrying a query or a path form the root cannot contain fails with its declared error code rather than being opened, while a reference carrying a scheme or an authority is emitted as authored, as the normalization fixtures show.
- [x] **AC7.** Each limit the profile names fails the compilation at the first boundary it crosses, with no bundle published and no content truncated, as the limit fixtures show.
- [x] **AC8.** Markdown classification recognizes the `.md` and `.markdown` suffixes case-insensitively, and an explicit entry carrying another suffix fails, as the suffix fixtures show.
- [x] **AC9.** The same selection produces the same bundle whatever order its entry references are given in and whatever order its dependencies were discovered in, with groups ordered by root-relative path, as the determinism fixtures show.
- [x] **AC11.** A target further from every entry reference than the declared expansion depth fails the run, as the depth fixtures show.
- [x] **AC12.** An image, a web URL or another non-Markdown reference in selected content is preserved without being opened, fetched or traversed as a dependency, as the resource-classification fixtures show.
- [x] **AC13.** Link ownership and direct-self-reference classification are the same before and after a selection is consolidated into a larger region, as the ownership fixtures show.
- [x] **AC14.** A filesystem path written as ordinary prose, rather than as a link, is left as text and resolved as no dependency, as the bare-text fixtures show.
- [x] **AC15.** An unmarked local Markdown link is emitted as authored, resolves as no dependency, and is left unrewritten even where the bundle carries the document it names, as the unmarked-link fixtures show.
- [x] **AC16.** A document whose unmarked references name material outside the allowed root bundles successfully, while marking one of them fails the run with its declared error code, as the citation fixtures show.

- [x] **AC17.** A marked reference naming a resource fails with its declared error code, while an unmarked one is emitted as authored, as the marked-resource fixtures show.

content.title: [I00:E05] Destination Identity: Renderer Fragments and Source-Local References
content.body:
## Overview

Destination identity makes the bundle navigable by name. Every included document and section takes as its destination the fragment the declared renderer generates for its bundled heading, every rewritten reference points at one, resolved reference-style links become inline links with their definitions removed, and a relative resource reference is carried as authored under a warning.

## Problem

Links that resolved in their source documents resolve to nothing once those documents are one document.

- **A heading slug is not unique across files.**
  Two documents can each hold a section whose heading produces the same slug, so a name derived from heading text alone cannot tell them apart.

- **A definition has file scope and the bundle has none.**
  A reference-style link resolves against its own document's definitions, so moving the use without its definition breaks it, and moving every definition into one document makes labels from different files compete.

- **An unresolved bracket is not a link.**
  Text one document leaves as literal brackets would become a link if another document's definition were in scope, which changes what the source said.

- **A relative resource path is relative to its source.**
  An image path that resolved from its source directory resolves from somewhere else once the content is published at a different location.

## Proposal

- **A destination is the fragment the renderer generates.**
  It is the bundled heading's slug, carrying the renderer's ordinal where two bundled headings share one, so every internal link resolves in a renderer, an editor preview and an agent reading the document whole. Nothing is emitted at the destination; the heading the renderer already indexes is the target.

- **A destination is scoped to the bundle.**
  The bundle is one document, so a section whose slug is unique in it needs no qualification and a cross-file reference is spelled like a same-file one. Two documents whose paths differ only by Markdown extension produce two file headings a reader cannot tell apart, and are refused.

- **The ordinal is safe because the bundle is generated.**
  In a source document an edit elsewhere would change how many similar headings precede a target and silently repoint a stored link. A bundle is written in one pass, validated against the map that produced it, never hand-edited and refused as input to a later run.

- **Every internal link points at its destination.**
  A local Markdown link and a fragment-only link in selected content are rewritten through the same map that produced the destination. A bundle whose destinations are right and whose links still name source paths is the failure this guards against.

- **Nothing is emitted at a destination.**
  The bundle carries Markdown and nothing else. A destination names a place in the document; it is not an element in it.

- **References resolve in their own source.**
  Reference-style uses are resolved against their own document's definition environment, converted to inline form with visible content and titles preserved, and every original definition node is removed, unused definitions included.

- **Literal brackets stay literal.**
  Text a source parser did not resolve as a link is emitted as literal text and cannot acquire a destination from another document's definitions.

- **A resource is text.**
  A relative image or other non-Markdown reference is emitted byte-identical to its source and never opened, rebased or resolved. Where a bundle will be read from is the caller's question, so the run warns that resource portability is not guaranteed rather than inventing a destination.

## Work Breakdown

| Task | Description | Coverage | Depends on | Joins | Done |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [W01](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/83) | Renderer-generated destinations and ambiguity | AC1, AC2 | [E03:W02](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/5) | | ✓ |
| [W02](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/86) | Link rewriting through the destination map | AC3, AC6 | W01, [E04:W04](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/6) | | ✓ |
| [W03](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/90) | Reference conversion and definition removal | AC4, AC5, AC7 | W02 | W04 | ✓ |
| [W04](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/90) | A reference naming an absorbed title | AC8 | W02 | W03 | ✓ |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **AC1.** Each included document and section carries as its destination the fragment the declared renderer generates for its bundled heading, taking the renderer's ordinal where two bundled headings share a slug, as the destination fixtures show.
- [x] **AC2.** Two headings in one source sharing a slug fail as ambiguous when a source fragment requires one of them, and two source paths differing only by Markdown extension fail as ambiguous, as the ambiguity fixtures show.
- [x] **AC3.** Each local Markdown link and fragment-only link in selected content is rewritten to the destination of the target it resolved to, and every destination in the published bundle resolves to exactly one heading in it, as the rewriting fixtures show.
- [x] **AC4.** A resolved reference-style link or image in selected content is published inline with its visible content and title preserved, and no original definition node is present, as the reference fixtures show.
- [x] **AC5.** Bracketed text a source parser left unresolved is published as literal text, as the literal-bracket fixtures show.
- [x] **AC6.** The bundle opens with a line naming each entry reference, linked by the visible text of the heading its destination names and resolving to that destination, stating that the remainder is material those entries reference, carrying no execution verb and counting toward no source's coverage, as the entry-line fixtures show.
- [x] **AC7.** A relative image or other non-Markdown reference is emitted byte-identical to its source, with a warning on the diagnostic stream that resource portability is not guaranteed, as the resource fixtures show.
- [x] **AC8.** A reference naming a source heading the file heading absorbed resolves to that file heading's destination, as the absorbed-title fixtures show.

content.title: [I00:E06] Candidate Validation: A Bundle Proven to Carry Its Sources
content.body:
## Overview

Candidate validation stands between a constructed candidate and a published bundle. The candidate is reparsed under the declared profile and checked against the provenance recorded during construction, and nothing reaches standard output until it passes. This is the one check that must precede first use: it establishes that what the tool hands a caller is the content its sources carried.

## Problem

A bundle can be syntactically valid Markdown and still be the wrong document.

- **Surface validity proves nothing about provenance.**
  A reparse that agrees with itself establishes that the output parses, not that each region came from the source it claims, nor that a region is missing.

- **A silent loss is worse than a failure.**
  A caller handed a bundle with a region missing proceeds on it, because nothing distinguishes a short bundle from a complete one. A caller handed a failure reads its sources another way.

## Proposal

- **Candidate validation has its own policy context.**
  The candidate is reparsed under the same grammar but expects generated filename headings, shifted headings and structural ancestors. It is not passed back through frontmatter stripping, dependency discovery or generated-input rejection.

- **Invariants are checked against recorded provenance.**
  Destination integrity, exactly-once coverage, absence of new links, absence of surviving definitions, ownership stability, outline preservation and depth safety are checked against the provenance ranges and generated-structure records kept during construction, not by counting strings.

- **A failing candidate publishes nothing.**
  Standard output stays empty and the run exits nonzero, so a caller cannot mistake a refused bundling for a short bundle.

- **The remaining gate follows first use.**
  Block boundary safety, source consistency, generated-input rejection, diagnostic content and validation scope extend this check rather than condition it, and are delivered by [E08](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/59) once the tool is in agents' hands.

## Work Breakdown

## Acceptance Criteria

content.title: [I00:E10] Corpus Conformance: The Contract Mapped to Executable Fixtures
content.body:
## Overview

Corpus conformance turns a passing build into a measured contract. The adversarial fixture families the design names are completed and every fixture the shipping epics declared but left awaiting this work is finished, every behavioural clause is mapped to the fixtures that exercise it, any clause no fixture covers is listed as uncovered, and the corpus and its report are checked for independence from any implementation. This is the artifact the production build inherits.

## Problem

A corpus that passes says what was tested, not what the contract requires.

- **Coverage is assumed, not measured.**
  Fixtures accumulate alongside the work that needed them, so a clause nobody implemented has no fixture and no record that it has none.

- **An absent fixture is invisible.**
  A clause with no fixture produces no failure, so the gap presents as a passing corpus.

- **Fixtures written beside one build inherit its assumptions.**
  A fixture naming a module, a flag spelling or an error-message wording specific to one implementation binds that implementation rather than the contract.

- **The adversarial cases are a list in prose.**
  The design names families of hard cases, and a family nobody turned into fixtures is a family the next implementation meets for the first time in production.

## Proposal

- **Each named family becomes fixtures.**
  Identity, coverage, destinations, references, extraction, boundaries, file hierarchy, partial outlines, normalization, resources, consistency, validation scope, generated inputs, delivery, parser fidelity, definition inventory, profile, frontmatter, command interface and limits each have fixtures in the corpus.

- **Clauses map to fixtures.**
  Each behavioural clause of the design carries the identifiers of the fixtures that exercise it. The mapping is generated from the corpus and the design rather than maintained by hand.

- **The declared names are exercised, not merely referred to.**
  The criteria bind to the error code and exit status the design declares rather than repeating the names, so nothing otherwise requires the build's set to be the design's. The report compares them, and a code the build emits that the design does not name, or a declared outcome no fixture produces, is a reported failure.

- **An uncovered clause is reported, not dropped.**
  A clause with no fixture appears in the report's uncovered list, so a gap is a visible result of running the report.

- **Independence is checked.**
  The corpus and the report are checked for references to an implementation language, module or internal error wording, so what they bind is the behaviour.

content.title: [I02] Production Compiler: The Contract Delivered in Rust
content.body:
## Overview

A Rust build of prosiform is the tool agents invoke, and it passes the fixture corpus without a fixture changing. It retains original source bytes and applies edits to identified spans, so untouched content and code examples survive bundling exactly. Before any of that work starts, the two parser viability gates the design names are answered by executed reproducers against a pinned parser version, with a recorded verdict and a recorded route for any gate the parser fails. The build targets one tagged revision of the design and corpus, so later refinement does not move the contract under it.

## Problem

A bundling the production build publishes must be trusted byte for byte, and the parser it rests on has not been proven able to supply that.

- **Reconstruction loses what the source said.**
  Regenerating a document through a formatter rewrites spacing, escaping and newline spelling, so bundled instructions and code examples stop being the bytes an author wrote.

- **A definition map holds one occurrence per label.**
  The inspected first pass inserts definitions with a first-wins entry, so a later duplicate occurrence has no map entry, and a source transformer removing definitions cannot find it.

- **A suppressed reference looks like ordinary text.**
  The inspected lookup returns nothing when its reference-expansion budget is zero, before definition lookup, so a reference the limit suppressed and bracketed text that was never a link reach the consumer identically.

- **The event range is not the destination range.**
  An enclosing event carries a span for the construct, not for the destination inside it, so an edit placed from that span alone can fall outside the text it means to replace.

- **An unpinned dependency changes the contract.**
  Parser behaviour on duplicate definitions, offsets and option-controlled extensions is what the profile rests on, so an unpinned upgrade can change how existing source is interpreted.

- **A contract read from a branch tip moves under the build.**
  Fixtures and design clauses that change while the build is written leave it satisfying no revision in particular.

## Proposal

- **The gates are answered before the build.**
  Executed reproducers establish whether the pinned parser exposes every reference-definition occurrence and whether it makes a suppressed reference lookup observable. Each answer and its evidence are recorded.

- **A failed gate takes a recorded route.**
  Parser-aware occurrence collection, narrowly scoped instrumentation, a different parser candidate and a separate upstream proposal are the routes. The route taken is a recorded decision, not an implicit fallback.

- **Edits are applied to verified spans.**
  Original bytes are retained and replaced in place. A construct whose exact edit span cannot be established fails rather than falling back to pattern rewriting or whole-document formatting.

- **The corpus is inherited, not rewritten.**
  The production build passes the fixtures established before the freeze. A fixture changing to accommodate the production build is a change to the contract and is decided as one.

- **One tagged revision is the target.**
  The work names the tagged revision of the design and corpus it implements, and adopting a later one is a recorded decision.

- **Both builds stay on one corpus.**
  A differential run bundles each corpus input with both builds and compares the results, so a divergence is a defect in one of them rather than a silent difference.

- **Versions are pinned after the fixtures pass.**
  The parser, the slugging component and every other dependency take exact versions, chosen once the fixtures hold against them.

## Work Breakdown

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [E00](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/11) | Parser Verdict | AC1 | | |
| [E01](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/12) | Source-Range Adapter | AC2, AC3, AC10 | [E00](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/11) | |
| [E02](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/13) | Profile and Outline | AC4 | [E00](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/11) | |
| [E03](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/14) | Closure and Budgets | AC5 | [E00](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/11) | |
| [E04](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/15) | Destination Identity | AC6 | [E00](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/11) | |
| [E05](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/16) | Validation and Delivery | AC7 | [E04](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/15) | |
| [E06](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/17) | Differential Conformance | AC8, AC9 | [E05](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/16) | |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** Each parser viability gate the design names has an executed reproducer and a recorded verdict against a pinned parser version, as the gate report shows.
- [ ] **AC2.** Untouched source bytes and their newline spelling survive bundling exactly, as the corpus's preservation fixtures and the span-fidelity fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC3.** A reference lookup an internal parser limit suppresses is observable to the compiler rather than indistinguishable from literal bracketed text, as the exhaustion fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC4.** A published bundle keeps the source outline and the declared Markdown profile, as the corpus's outline and profile fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC5.** A bundling resolves its dependency closure and holds every limit the profile names, as the corpus's closure and limit fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC6.** A published bundle carries one destination per rewritten reference and no original reference definition, as the corpus's destination and reference fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC7.** A bundling that fails validation publishes nothing, exits nonzero and writes its diagnostic, as the corpus's failure fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC8.** Both builds produce identical output for each corpus input, as the differential run shows.
- [ ] **AC9.** Every dependency is pinned to an exact version against which the corpus passes, as the lockfile and that run show.
- [ ] **AC10.** The build implements one tagged revision of the design and corpus, as the recorded target revision and the corpus run against it show.

## Non-Goals

- It does not open an issue or a pull request on another project.
- It does not disable a parser resource protection to satisfy a gate.
- It does not rewrite a corpus fixture to accommodate the production build without a recorded decision.
- It does not replace the prototype, which stays in use as the differential oracle.
- It does not fetch remote documents, resources or URLs.
- It does not accept its own output as a source document.

## References

content.title: [I02:E00] Parser Verdict: Viability Gates Tested Against a Pinned Parser
content.body:
## Overview

The parser verdict answers, with executed reproducers against a pinned parser version, whether that parser can supply what the design requires: access to every reference-definition occurrence, and an observable signal when an internal limit suppresses a reference lookup. The epic ends with a report stating each gate's answer and the evidence behind it, and a recorded route for any gate the parser fails.

## Problem

The production build rests on parser capabilities that have been inspected in source but never executed.

- **A definition map holds one occurrence per label.**
  The inspected first pass inserts definitions with a first-wins entry, so a later duplicate occurrence becomes no map entry, and removing every definition from emitted content requires finding occurrences the map does not hold.

- **A suppressed lookup is indistinguishable from literal text.**
  The inspected lookup returns nothing once its reference-expansion budget reaches zero, before definition lookup and before broken-link handling, so a reference the limit suppressed and brackets that were never a link arrive identically.

- **A retained definition does not imply enumerable duplicates.**
  Exposure of the winning definition map is evidence about resolution, not about occurrence coverage, so the gate cannot be answered by reading that interface.

- **Agreement between two parses proves nothing about omission.**
  An event stream that omits a suppressed reference omits it consistently, so a second parse agrees with the first and the omission stays invisible.

- **An upstream fix of unknown reach.**
  An offset-iterator defect on definition-bearing list items is reported upstream with a fix described on the project's main line, and which released version carries it has not been established here.

## Proposal

- **Each gate gets an executed reproducer.**
  One constructs sources carrying later duplicate definitions, case-fold-equivalent labels, unused definitions, multiline definitions and supported container contexts, and records what the pinned parser's public interface exposes for each. One drives reference-expansion suppression below the tool's declared input and output limits and records whether the suppression is observable.

- **A budget exhausted on a final successful reference is a distinct case.**
  The suppression reproducer includes a source whose last valid reference consumes the budget with no later lookup, because reporting that as an omission would fail runs that omitted nothing.

- **The reported offset-iterator defect is executed, not assumed.**
  Its reproducer runs against the pinned version, and the result is recorded against the existing upstream report rather than becoming a new one.

- **Resource protections stay on.**
  No gate is answered by disabling a parser limit. A reproducer that would need that records the gate as unsatisfied.

- **A failed gate takes a recorded route.**
  Parser-aware occurrence collection, narrowly scoped instrumentation, a different parser candidate and a separate upstream proposal are the routes. The route taken is written into the report as a decision with its reasoning.

## Work Breakdown

| [W02](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/tree/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-10-17-prosiform-v1/i02-e00/w02.md) | Reference-suppression reproducer | AC2, AC3 | | | |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC2.** A reproducer drives reference-expansion suppression below the tool's declared input and output limits and records whether that suppression is observable through the pinned parser's public interface, as its recorded run shows.

content.title: [I02:E01] Source-Range Adapter: Spans Verified and Edits Applied
content.body:
## Overview

The source-range adapter is what lets the production build edit a document without rewriting it. It pairs parser events with verified source ranges, maps those ranges back to original bytes through every preprocessing step, and applies non-overlapping edits in place, so untouched content and code examples remain the bytes their authors wrote.

## Problem

An event's range is not the range an edit needs, and the mapping between the parser's view and the original file is not the identity.

- **An enclosing range is not a destination range.**
  A link event carries a span for the construct, so an edit placed from that span replaces more than the destination, or falls outside it.

- **Preprocessing moves every offset.**
  A removed byte-order mark and stripped frontmatter shift the parser's view relative to the file, so a diagnostic or an edit computed in one coordinate space lands wrong in the other.

- **Line endings, tabs and escapes are not one byte each.**
  A range expressed in the parser's view maps to a different extent in the original when carriage returns, expanded tabs, escapes or multi-byte characters sit inside it.

- **Nested constructs produce overlapping edits.**
  An image inside a link has two destinations whose edits overlap, so applying both independently corrupts the construct.

- **A missing span has no safe fallback.**
  Pattern rewriting or regenerating the document through a formatter would change bytes nobody selected.

## Proposal

- **Spans are verified, not assumed.**
  Each construct the design edits has its exact source range established by fixture before it is relied on: headings, link and image uses, and reference definitions.

- **Coordinates map both ways.**
  A range in the parser's view maps to original UTF-8 byte offsets through the recorded preprocessing, and diagnostics report original source coordinates.

- **Nested edits take a parent strategy.**
  A construct containing another is edited as one replacement built from both, rather than as two overlapping edits.

- **An unavailable span fails.**
  A construct whose edit span cannot be established fails the run with a diagnostic. There is no pattern-rewriting or whole-document-formatting path.

- **The crate comes before the adapter.**
  This epic creates the production tree, its workspace, its pinned toolchain and the same documented check commands the prototype carries, so the adapter is written into a build that already runs its own checks. Nothing earlier creates that tree, so it appears when there is a build to put in it.

- **Suppression reaches the compiler.**
  The signal the gate report establishes is wired through the adapter, so a reference lookup an internal limit suppressed is distinguishable from literal bracketed text.

## Work Breakdown

| Task | Description | Coverage | Depends on | Joins | Done |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| W00 | Production tree, workspace and toolchain | AC7 | [E00:W04](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/11) | | |
| W01 | Verified spans and coordinate mapping | AC1, AC2, AC6 | W00, [I01:E02:W02](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/23) | | |
| W02 | Non-overlapping edit application | AC3, AC4 | W01 | | |
| W03 | Suppression signal wired to the compiler | AC5 | W01 | | |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** Each construct the design edits has its exact source range established, as the span-fidelity fixtures covering multiline references, reference-style images, tables, tabs, escapes, Unicode and carriage-return line endings show.
- [ ] **AC2.** A diagnostic reports original source coordinates after byte-order-mark and frontmatter preprocessing, as the coordinate fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC3.** Bytes outside an applied edit, code examples and newline spelling included, are identical to their source, as the preservation fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC4.** A construct containing another is replaced as one edit rather than as overlapping edits, as the nested image-in-link fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC5.** A reference lookup an internal parser limit suppresses fails the run with its declared error code rather than being published as literal text, as the exhaustion fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC6.** The work names the tagged revision of the design and corpus it implements, as the recorded target revision shows.
- [ ] **AC7.** A fresh checkout builds the production crate from its own tree and runs its tests, lint, format and type checks from documented commands at a pinned toolchain, as the continuous-integration run shows.

## Open Questions

content.title: [I02:E02] Profile and Outline: The Declared Grammar and Heading Hierarchy
content.body:
## Overview

Profile and outline bring the production build to the point where it bundles one document correctly: the declared Markdown profile configured explicitly, a compatibility-tested source-heading slugger, eligible section extraction, the group heading shift with title absorption and Setext conversion, heading-only structural ancestors, and the grouping rules that merge one part of the tree. The corpus's profile and outline fixtures are what it is measured against.

## Problem

The production build starts with no profile, no slugger and no section model, and each of them changes how existing source is read.

- **A default parser configuration is not the declared profile.**
  Enabling everything available, or accepting defaults, changes whether a construct is a table, a strikethrough, a task marker or ordinary text.

- **A fragment is renderer-defined.**
  The fragment reaching a heading is generated from its visible text and its duplicate numbering, and no slugging component is selected yet.

- **A heading inside a container is still a heading.**
  It must shift with the rest and must not terminate the section that encloses it, which the extraction and shift rules treat as separate facts.

- **Setext headings have no prefix to edit.**
  Shifting one means converting it, which an edit-in-place build must do without disturbing its inline content.

- **A grouping rule moves a member's sections out of its own outline.**
  Merging documents at a heading level puts their sections under one shared outline, so a name two members both carry needs a place for both, and a member's content above that level needs a place of its own.

## Proposal

- **Options are set explicitly and pinned with the profile identifier.**
  Pipe tables and strikethrough on, source task markers preserved, typographic substitution off, unsupported extensions off.

- **A slugging component is selected against the compatibility fixtures.**
  The fixtures decide, not the component's documentation, and the chosen version is pinned.

- **The section model comes from the event stream.**
  Eligible roots, boundaries, container nesting and heading ancestry are derived from events with their verified ranges, and heading syntax is edited rather than regenerated.

- **Structural ancestors are generated structure.**
  Unselected ancestors are emitted as escaped literal headings, recorded separately from selected content, and not traversed.

- **A grouping rule merges one part of the tree, and names stay verbatim.**
  Every document under a named directory is merged at a source heading level beneath one heading carrying that directory's slug in title case. A merged name occurring once is emitted bare; one several members carry is emitted once with a variant heading per member. Each member's content above the grouping depth is held in the group's overview section.

## Work Breakdown

| Task | Description | Coverage | Depends on | Joins | Done |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| W01 | Profile configuration and slugger selection | AC1, AC2 | [E01:W01](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/12) | | |
| W02 | Section extraction and heading shift | AC3, AC4 | W01, [E01:W02](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/12) | | |
| W03 | Structural ancestors and depth overflow | AC5, AC6 | W02 | | |
| W04 | Grouping, variants and the overview section | AC7, AC8, AC9 | W03 | | |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** The parser is configured to the declared profile, with typographic substitution absent and source task markers preserved, as the corpus's profile fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC2.** A source heading's fragment equals the one a GitHub renderer generates for it, as the corpus's slug compatibility fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC3.** A fragment selects its eligible section and the blocks up to the next document-level heading of equal or higher level, as the corpus's extraction fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC4.** Each emitted source heading sits exactly one level deeper than in its source with its visible text unchanged, Setext headings included, while a group whose title the file heading absorbs keeps its source levels, as the corpus's shift fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC5.** A selected section's unselected eligible ancestors are emitted as headings carrying no body, sibling or descendant content, as the corpus's structural ancestor fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC6.** A bundling that would place a heading beyond the sixth level fails with its declared error code, as the corpus's depth-overflow fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC7.** One entry bundled with and without a group selects the same content and differs only in how it is arranged, with each group emitting one heading carrying its slug in title case, a merged section emitted once however many member documents contribute to it, and a document no group names keeping its own group, as the corpus's grouping fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC8.** A merged heading occurring once in its group is emitted with its source text alone, while one drawn from several documents is emitted once with each document's content beneath a variant heading naming that document, and a merged section carrying body text from more than one document splits into variants by document, and a member's content above the grouping depth is emitted under the group's overview section as a subsection named by that document's stem in title case less a trailing word the section states, as the corpus's grouping fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC9.** A grouping rule whose depth falls outside the supported heading levels, whose slug names no directory under the root, or whose slug is given twice is refused with its declared error code and exit status, as the corpus's grouping fixtures show.

## Open Questions

- Whether the rows above hold at this grain, and the work item for each, settled once the gate report is recorded.
- Whether the slugging component is an existing crate or an implementation in this repository, decided by which passes the compatibility fixtures.

content.title: [I02:E03] Closure and Budgets: Recursive Resolution Under Enforced Limits
content.body:
## Overview

Closure and budgets bring the production build from one document to a compiled dependency graph: reference normalization, root confinement without following symbolic links, recursive traversal to a fixed point, overlap consolidation, self- and ancestor-reference classification, and every resource limit the profile names. The corpus's closure and limit fixtures are what it is measured against.

## Problem

Confinement and termination are properties of the access path and the traversal, and neither survives being assumed.

- **A string check is not confinement.**
  A path validated before opening can still reach outside the root through a symbolic link resolved at open time.

- **A reference graph has cycles.**
  Instruction sets link back to one another, so a traversal without a fixed point repeats regions or does not terminate.

- **The same region arrives by several paths.**
  A section selected directly and again inside a later whole-document inclusion is one region.

- **An unbounded compilation fails late.**
  Without enforced budgets, a pathological tree is discovered by exhausting memory rather than by a diagnostic.

- **Parser nesting limits can reinterpret syntax.**
  A limit expressed only as a parser option can cause over-deep syntax to be read as something else rather than failing.

## Proposal

- **Access is rooted and no-follow.**
  Confinement is enforced by the access mechanism, and a platform unable to enforce it declares a narrower supported environment rather than weakening the policy.

- **Normalization follows the declared sequence.**
  Components split before decoding, escapes validate strictly, decoding happens once, and relative segments normalize against the proper base.

- **Traversal runs to a fixed point with consolidation.**
  Newly included content is traversed, and a larger region replaces the narrower selections inside it.

- **Identity decides self-reference.**
  Comparison happens after canonical path and fragment resolution, and link ownership is stored separately from inclusion so consolidation cannot change the classification.

- **Nesting fails explicitly.**
  The declared nesting limit is enforced as a failure of this build, not left to the parser's own reinterpretation.

## Work Breakdown

| Task | Description | Coverage | Depends on | Joins | Done |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| W01 | Normalization and rooted no-follow access | AC1, AC2 | [E01:W01](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/12) | | |
| W02 | Traversal, consolidation and reference identity | AC3, AC4, AC5 | W01, [E02:W02](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/13) | | |
| W03 | Resource budgets and nesting enforcement | AC6, AC7 | W02 | | |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** A local Markdown reference carrying a query, an unsupported scheme or an unsupported path form fails with its declared error code, as the corpus's normalization fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC2.** A reference whose normalized path leaves the allowed root, or reaches a source through a symbolic link below it, fails with its declared error code, as the corpus's confinement fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC3.** A cyclic reference graph bundles to a fixed point with each reachable region present once, as the corpus's cycle fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC4.** A selection contained within a larger selection is represented by the larger region alone, with that region's own references resolved, as the corpus's consolidation fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC5.** A link to the same canonical section fails as a direct self-reference while a link back to an including ancestor resolves to that ancestor's destination, as the corpus's self-reference fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC6.** Each limit the profile names fails the compilation at the first boundary it crosses, with nothing published and nothing truncated, as the corpus's limit fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC7.** Syntax exceeding the declared nesting limit fails rather than being read as different syntax, as the corpus's nesting fixtures show.

## Open Questions

- Whether the rows above hold at this grain, and the work item for each, settled once the gate report is recorded.
- Which rooted no-follow access mechanism the supported platforms provide, and whether any platform must be declared unsupported as a result.

## References
