content.title: [I02:E04] Destination Identity: Renderer Fragments, Definitions and Resource Rebasing
content.body:
## Overview

Destination identity in the production build names each included document and section by the fragment the declared renderer generates for its bundled heading, converts resolved reference-style uses to inline form while removing every original definition occurrence, and rebases relative resource references. It is the epic where the definition-occurrence gate's route becomes code.

## Problem

Removing a reference definition requires finding every occurrence of it, which is the capability the first parser gate questions.

- **A later duplicate definition has no map entry.**
  First-definition-wins resolution means the map holds one occurrence per label, while emission must remove them all.

- **An unused definition still occupies source.**
  It resolves nothing and must still be absent from bundled content.

- **Labels equivalent under case folding are one label.**
  Occurrence removal that compares labels literally leaves equivalents behind.

- **Fragments collide across files.**
  Two documents can each produce the same fragment, so one bundle carrying both needs destinations that distinguish them.

- **A relative resource path is relative to its source.**
  Publishing the content elsewhere changes what that path reaches.

## Proposal

- **Occurrence access follows the recorded route.**
  Whatever route the gate report names is what supplies the occurrence inventory, and removal is driven from that inventory rather than from the resolution map.

- **A destination is the fragment the renderer generates.**
  The bundled heading's slug, carrying the renderer's ordinal where two bundled headings share one, assigned by walking the emitted headings in bundle order. Every internal link then resolves wherever the bundle is read.

- **A source fragment still names one heading.**
  Two headings in one source producing one slug make a source fragment ambiguous, so a reference requiring one of them fails and the author retitles. The ordinal belongs to the bundle, which the tool generates, not to a source it only reads.

- **Literal brackets stay literal.**
  Text no source parser resolved as a link cannot acquire a destination from another document's definitions.

- **Resources rebase or fail.**
  A reference that cannot be rebased safely fails rather than acquiring an invented destination.

## Work Breakdown

| Task | Description | Coverage | Depends on | Joins | Done |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| W01 | Renderer-generated destinations and link rewriting | AC1, AC2 | [E02:W02](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/13) | | |
| W02 | Entry line and merged-reference resolution | AC5, AC6 | W01 | | |
| W03 | Definition occurrence removal and inline conversion | AC3, AC4 | W02, [E03:W02](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/14) | | |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** Each included document and section is named by the fragment the declared renderer generates for its bundled heading, taking the renderer's ordinal where two bundled headings share a slug, as the corpus's destination fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC2.** Every cross-file and fragment-only link in selected content is rewritten to the destination of the target it resolved to, and two sibling headings producing one slug fail as ambiguous, as the corpus's destination fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC3.** No original reference definition occurrence survives in published content, later duplicates, unused labels, case-fold-equivalent labels, multiline definitions and supported container contexts included, as the corpus's definition-inventory fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC4.** A resolved reference-style use is published inline with its visible content and title preserved, while bracketed text no parser resolved stays literal, as the corpus's reference fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC5.** Under a grouping rule, a reference to a source heading at the grouping depth resolves to the variant heading carrying the document it named, and to the merged heading itself where that name occurs once, as the corpus's grouping fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC6.** The bundle opens with a line naming each entry reference, linked by the visible text of the heading its destination names and resolving to that destination, stating that the remainder is material those entries reference, carrying no execution verb and counting toward no source's coverage, as the corpus's entry-line fixtures show.

## Open Questions

- Whether the rows above hold at this grain, and the work item for each, settled once the gate report is recorded.
- Whether the occurrence inventory comes from the parser's public interface, from scoped instrumentation or from a different parser, decided by the gate report.

## References

content.title: [I02:E05] Validation and Delivery: Candidate Checks, Diagnostics and Publication
content.body:
## Overview

Validation and delivery close the production build: the candidate validation mode and its provenance invariants, boundary safety, source-change detection, generated-input rejection, the diagnostic shape and its JSON form, the command interface, and the delivery contract that makes a partial transport a reported failure rather than an apparent success.

## Problem

A compilation that validated is not yet a bundle the calling agent received.

- **Surface validity proves nothing about provenance.**
  A candidate that parses can still omit a selected region or carry a destination that points somewhere else.

- **A boundary can swallow what follows it.**
  Regions joined without safe separation can place later content inside an earlier fence, HTML block, list or quote.

- **Standard output is not an atomic delivery.**
  A broken pipe or a transport limit can truncate a bundle that compiled correctly, and Markdown arriving is not evidence that all of it arrived.

- **A failure the agent cannot explain is a failure twice.**
  Without a code, a location, the offending reference and the inclusion chain, a calling agent can report only that bundling failed.

## Proposal

- **Candidate mode has its own policy context.**
  Generated filename headings, shifted headings and structural ancestors are expected; frontmatter stripping, dependency discovery and generated-input rejection do not run on the candidate.

- **Invariants are checked against recorded provenance.**
  Destination integrity, exactly-once coverage, absence of new links, absence of surviving definitions, ownership stability, outline preservation and depth safety are checked against provenance ranges and generated-structure records.

- **Publication is atomic and gated.**
  File output is written atomically after validation, and an output that would overwrite an input source is refused.

- **Delivery failure is reported, not disguised.**
  A detected broken pipe or write failure returns its declared exit status, and no oversized output is replaced with a summary or a partial document.

- **Diagnostics carry a stable shape.**
  Code, referring source location, original reference, resolved identity where one exists, inclusion chain and a remedy where one can be stated accurately, with one JSON object per line when that format is selected.

## Work Breakdown

| Task | Description | Coverage | Depends on | Joins | Done |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| W01 | Candidate validation and boundary safety | AC1, AC2 | [E04:W03](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/15) | | |
| W02 | Source consistency and generated-input rejection | AC3 | W01 | | |
| W03 | Command interface, diagnostics and exit statuses | AC4, AC5, AC8 | W02 | | |
| W04 | Atomic publication and delivery failure | AC6, AC7 | W03 | | |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** A candidate disagreeing with its recorded source provenance publishes nothing and fails, as the corpus's validation fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC2.** A region boundary that would place content inside an unintended container fails with its declared error code, as the corpus's boundary fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC3.** A source whose content or canonical identity changes during compilation fails with a retry diagnostic, and a source whose links carry bundle destinations is rejected, as the corpus's consistency and generated-input fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC4.** Each diagnostic carries a stable error code, the referring source location, the original reference, the resolved identity where one exists and the inclusion chain, as the corpus's diagnostic fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC5.** The command returns the declared exit status for each outcome the design names, as the corpus's exit-status fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC6.** A detected broken output pipe or write failure returns its declared exit status rather than reporting success, and no bundle is replaced by a summary or a partial document, as the corpus's delivery fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC7.** A successful run reports each entry reference and the destination it resolved to on the diagnostic stream, under a grouping rule as without one, as the corpus's delivery fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC8.** A validation-only run bundles and validates its entry references and publishes nothing, to either stream or to a named output file, as the corpus's check fixtures show.

## Open Questions

- Whether the rows above hold at this grain, and the work item for each, settled once the gate report is recorded.
- Whether validation-mode reparsing reuses the adapter's recorded ranges or reparses the candidate independently, decided once the adapter's cost against the corpus is measured.

content.title: [I02:E06] Differential Conformance: Both Builds on One Corpus
content.body:
## Overview

Differential conformance makes the two builds check each other. Both bundle every corpus input in continuous integration, their outputs are compared, every dependency takes an exact pinned version, and the result is the released production tool with the prototype retained as its oracle.

## Problem

Two implementations of one contract diverge quietly unless something compares them.

- **A corpus tests what it declares.**
  A behaviour no fixture declares can differ between the builds without any fixture failing.

- **An unpinned dependency changes the contract.**
  Parser behaviour on duplicate definitions, offsets and option-controlled extensions is what the profile rests on, so an unpinned upgrade can change how existing source is interpreted.

- **A fixture rewritten to pass hides a defect.**
  Changing an expectation so the production build passes converts a defect into a contract change, without a record that the contract changed.

- **A passing build is not a released tool.**
  Without a build that agents can invoke, the work stops at a repository.

## Proposal

- **Both builds run every input.**
  The differential run bundles each corpus input with both builds and compares the results byte for byte, so a divergence outside the declared expectations is still a failure.

- **Pins come after the fixtures pass.**
  Exact versions are chosen once the corpus holds against them, and the lockfile is what the run uses.

- **A fixture change is a decision.**

- **The prototype stays.**
  It is maintained as the oracle rather than removed once the production build passes.

content.title: [I00:E07] Field Deployment: The Prototype Invoked by Agents
content.body:
## Overview

Field deployment makes the prototype the tool agents invoke. It installs with a stable entry point, a wrapper owns the delivery contract so a bundle arrives whole or is reported as a delivery failure, and the invocation is documented where the callers that use it live. Without this epic the build is a passing corpus rather than something in use.

## Problem

A validated build nobody can invoke changes nothing, and standard output alone does not establish that a bundle arrived.

- **The command runs only from a checkout.**
  Nothing installs it or names an entry point a caller can depend on, so every caller resolves the build's location for itself.

- **Standard output is not an atomic delivery.**
  A transport limit or a broken pipe can truncate a bundle that compiled correctly, and Markdown arriving is not evidence that all of it arrived.

- **Success read from output accepts a failure.**
  A caller treating the presence of Markdown as success accepts a failed run whose diagnostics went to the other stream.

- **A result field is not guaranteed to reach the agent.**
  The delivery contract guarantees the bundle arrives whole. It guarantees nothing about what a transport does with metadata beside it, so a destination returned only in a structured result may never enter the context that holds the document it describes.

- **An undocumented invocation is used inconsistently.**
  Each caller invents its own arguments, so a bundling that fails for one caller is not reproducible for another.

## Proposal

- **The build installs with a stable entry point.**
  One documented command name, resolvable without knowing where the repository sits.

- **A wrapper owns the delivery contract.**
  It checks process status, buffers the bundle, enforces the transport's response limit, and returns a delivery failure rather than a truncated success. It never substitutes a summary, a partial document or a reference the caller must follow.

- **Metadata stays out of the bundle.**
  Completion metadata, byte counts and warnings belong in the wrapper's structured result, not in the Markdown and not in per-section envelopes.

- **The run reports where the entry landed.**
  Each entry reference and the destination it resolved to are reported on the diagnostic stream, so a caller can act on them as data. What reaches the agent is the bundle's own entry line, which says the same thing in the document the agent reads.

- **Invocation is documented where callers are.**
  The entry point's options, defaults, exit statuses and profile identifier are documented in the repository, checked against the command's own help output.

- **A failed run stops the work.**
  There is no supported path by which a caller meeting a failure reads the sources itself instead. Falling back would restore the behaviour bundling replaces, and would do it silently, so the failure would teach nothing.

| [W03](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/99) | Documented invocation for callers | AC4, AC5 | W02, [E06:W01](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/8) | | ✓ |
| [W04](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/67) | A released version reported from the entry point | AC1 | W01 | | ✓ |

- [x] **AC3.** A failed run is reported from the process status rather than from the presence of Markdown on standard output, as the wrapper's unit cases and the delivery fixture for a failing run show.
- [x] **AC4.** The repository documents the entry point's options, defaults, exit statuses and profile identifier, as the documentation check against the command's own help output shows.

content.title: [I01:E00] Findings Ledger: Surprises From Use Recorded and Reproducible
content.body:
## Overview

The ledger is where what use reveals is kept, and the capture tool is what makes an entry something that can be re-run. Together they turn a surprise met while bundling into evidence a revision can be judged against.

## Problem

A finding met mid-task competes with the task, and a finding stated in words cannot be re-run.

- **The cheapest action is a local workaround.**
  The agent is carrying out a procedure, so without a recorded place for a surprise the surprise is absorbed and the design keeps its original claim.

- **Prose is not reproducible.**
  A finding described in sentences cannot establish whether a later change fixed it, so the question becomes a matter of opinion.

- **An untriaged entry is a backlog item.**
  An entry nobody classifies never reaches the design, the corpus or the build, and accumulates instead.

- **A real source tree is not a fixture.**
  The skill tree that triggered a surprise is too large to serve as a fixture and carries content the finding does not need.

## Proposal

- **The ledger is a file in the planning record.**
  Each entry carries its date, the invocation, the source identities it bundled, the observed result and the result expected.

- **Triage is part of the entry.**
  One state among design change, corpus gap, build defect and no change, with the reason for it. A schema check validates every entry.

- **A capture tool reduces an entry to a fixture.**
  It takes the invocation and the source closure the entry reached and emits the smallest fixture directory and manifest that still reproduces the observed result.

- **The ledger records runs, not only surprises.**
  Each bundling run is recorded with the source identities it bundled and its outcome, and a surprise entry cites the run it came from. A ledger holding only surprises cannot show whether the tool was used.

- **A run records whether the entry was found.**
  The bundle names what it was built for in its entry line, and whether that is enough is a question about agent behaviour that no reading of the design settles. Each run records whether the entry's content was acted on from the bundle alone, so the arrangement has evidence rather than argument behind it.

- **A run is measured against what it replaces.**
  Each run record carries the bundled output size and the total size of the same sources read whole, so the retrieval cost the proposal measured has a bundled figure to sit beside.

- **The exposure set is declared once.**
  It names the real sources the tool must have bundled before the specification can be called settled, and it is written down at the start of the stage rather than chosen at its end.

- **A reduced fixture waits with its entry.**
  It enters the corpus with the revision that resolves the entry, so the corpus never carries a fixture declared to fail.

## Work Breakdown

| [W02](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/tree/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-10-17-prosiform-v1/i01-e00/w02.md) | Fixture capture from a recorded entry | AC3, AC4 | W01 | | |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC2.** Each entry carries one of the declared triage states with its reason, as the schema check shows.

- [ ] **AC4.** A reduced fixture carries no source the observed result does not need, as the reduction tests show.

content.title: [I01:E01] Specification Revision: The Design Changed by What Use Showed
content.body:
## Overview

Specification revision is the order an accepted finding travels in and the revisions that travel it. The design changes first, the corpus follows, and the build follows the corpus. A finding accepted after this epic opens becomes a further row of it, so the refinement that remains is visible rather than implied.

## Problem

A correction applied in the wrong place leaves the contract wrong and the next implementation reading it.

- **A fix in the build leaves the design asserting the original behaviour.**
  The design is what a second implementation reads, so a bundling corrected only in code carries its correction nowhere.

- **A corpus changed first makes the design follow the fixtures.**
  A fixture edited to match an observed result turns an accident into the contract.

- **A revision with no trace cannot be reviewed.**
  A design change whose motivating finding is not recorded reads as an unexplained edit.

- **A clause added under refinement has no fixture.**
  It produces no failure, so the gap presents as a passing corpus.

- **An unbounded refinement has no visible end.**
  Without a measure of what remains open, there is no way to judge how close the specification is to settling.

## Proposal

- **Design, then corpus, then build.**
  An accepted finding changes the design clause it contradicts; the corpus gains or amends the fixture that would have caught it; the prototype changes until that fixture passes.

- **Each revision cites its finding.**
  The design and corpus revision history names the ledger entry that motivated the change.

- **Traceability is refreshed with each revision.**
  The clause-to-fixture mapping is regenerated whenever the design or the corpus changes, so a clause added without a fixture appears as uncovered on the revision that added it.

- **An accepted finding becomes a row.**
  Rows are added to this epic as findings are accepted, each covering the criterion stating what resolving it makes true.

- **A prerequisite section goes when bundling replaces it.**
  A skill's prerequisite section names whole documents, coarsely but completely, and the inline links inside a procedure name sections precisely but may not cover everything that list covered. Removal is therefore gated on a recorded bundling supplying what the list named, and a shortfall is a ledger entry rather than a silent loss.

- **The instruction replaces the list.**
  Where a section said which documents to read, the skill's own text says which invocation bundles them. The agent is told to bundle rather than left to infer it, and how clearly that reads is itself something use reports.

- **What remains open is reported from the ledger.**
  The summary is derived rather than maintained, so it cannot drift from the entries it describes.

## Work Breakdown

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC2.** Each design and corpus revision cites the ledger entry that motivated it, as the revision-order check shows.

- [ ] **AC4.** The entries awaiting resolution are reported from the ledger, grouped by triage state, as the open-finding summary shows.

content.title: [I01:E02] Specification Freeze: The Tagged Revision the Build Targets
content.body:
## Overview

The freeze is what ends the refinement stage and gives a production build something fixed to implement. Every ledger entry is resolved or explicitly deferred, a check refuses the freeze while one is neither, and the design and corpus take one tagged revision that a later build names as its target.

## Problem

A specification still accumulating changes cannot be implemented against, and a stage with no deferral path cannot end.

- **An open finding and a settled contract cannot both hold.**
  A corpus that still changes gives a second implementation no revision it can be said to satisfy.

- **An unused tool reports no problems.**
  A condition counting only recorded findings is satisfied by a ledger nobody wrote in, so it holds on the first day of the stage with the specification exactly as unexamined as when it started.

- **One awkward finding can hold the stage open indefinitely.**
  Without a deferral path, a single unresolved entry blocks the freeze regardless of its weight.

- **A revision with no name cannot be targeted.**
  A build that follows the branch tip follows later refinement rather than the specification it was reviewed against.

- **A silently dropped entry reappears later.**
  An entry closed without a reason is met again by whoever next encounters the behaviour.

## Proposal

- **Deferral is a decision with a reason.**
  An entry still open at the freeze names what is deferred and why. It stays in the ledger for the stage that takes it rather than being closed.

- **A check gates the tag.**
  The freeze is refused while any entry is neither resolved nor deferred, so the tag cannot be applied over an unexamined ledger.

- **An empty ledger is not a settled contract.**
  The freeze is also refused until every source in the declared exposure set has a recorded bundling run, so a specification cannot be called settled because nobody exercised it.

- **One tagged revision covers design and corpus.**
  Both take the same revision, so the contract and the fixtures that bind it cannot be targeted separately.

- **A later revision is adopted by decision.**
  A production build names the tag it targets, and moving to a later one is recorded rather than inherited.

## Work Breakdown

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC3.** The design and the corpus carry one tagged revision, as the tag shows.
- [ ] **AC4.** The freeze check refuses a tag until each source in the declared exposure set carries a recorded bundling run, as its tests show.

content.title: [I00:E00] Project Foundation: The Repository Laid Out and Checked
content.body:
## Overview

The repository holds a placeholder and nothing else. This epic lays out the trees this stage needs, establishes a Python environment whose dependencies resolve to pinned versions, makes tests and static checks runnable from documented commands that continuous integration also runs, and states in the README what the project is. Every later task lands in the structure it creates.

## Problem

The plan assumes a repository that does not exist yet, so its first task has nowhere to land.

- **The default branch is a placeholder.**
  `main` holds a README whose body is `tbd` and no other file, so there is no tree, no package and no test to extend.

- **The planned layout lives only in a decision.**
  The record names separate trees for the fixture corpus and the Python build, and nothing in the repository realizes that separation.

- **Nothing pins what the build runs on.**
  The prototype's parser is decided and unpinned, so two checkouts can resolve different parser versions and disagree about what a document means.

- **Tests have no runner.**
  Every later epic carries tests, and nothing states how they are discovered, how they are run, or what reports a failure.

- **A reader finds no account of the project.**
  The design and the plan sit on another branch, and nothing in the default branch says what the tool is or points at them.

- **The contract's vocabulary lives nowhere a user can read it.**
  The design names a closure, a region, a structural ancestor, a variant and a destination, each meaning one thing and nothing else. A reader of the tool meets those words in its diagnostics and its documentation with no definition to hand, and a later author has nothing to keep the usage from drifting.

## Proposal

- **The trees this stage needs.**
  One tree for the language-neutral fixture corpus, one for the Python build, and one for the documentation the repository owns. The production build's tree, toolchain and dependencies are created by the initiative that writes that build, so nothing here stands empty waiting for it.

- **One Python environment, resolved to pinned versions.**
  A project definition declares the runtime version and the dependencies, and a lockfile records the exact resolved versions a checkout installs, so parser behaviour does not vary between checkouts.

- **Documented commands run the checks.**
  Tests, lint, format and type checks are each a named command. Continuous integration runs those same commands rather than its own variants, so a check cannot pass locally and be absent remotely.

- **The README is the way in.**
  What the tool does, how it is installed, how it is invoked, and links to the design and the plan on the branch that holds them.

- **The glossary ships with the tool.**
  One definition for each term the contract uses, in the documentation tree, published with the build rather than kept in the planning record. The design, the acceptance criteria, the corpus and the tool's diagnostics draw their vocabulary from it, so a term means one thing across all four.

- **Documentation is linked, not copied.**
  The documentation tree holds what the repository owns. The design and the planning record stay on the engineering branch and are referenced, so there is one copy of each.

## Work Breakdown

| [W04](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/37) | Continuous integration running those commands | AC4 | W03 | | ✓ |

content.title: [I00:E11] Deferred Debt: The Defects This Initiative Delivered Past
content.body:
## Overview

This epic holds the technical debt the prototype initiative's delivery defers. A unit that finds debt while validating its work fixes it when it blocks the unit's own criteria or needs no work item of its own, and defers it here when it blocks nothing and would warrant a work item. The epic runs after every other epic of the initiative, so the clear-up competes with none of them, and each deferred item is one row covering the criterion that states what fixing it makes true.

## Problem

Debt found during delivery has nowhere to go that is neither a widened epic nor an orphan.

- **Widening the epic in hand changes what it was planned to be.**
  A unit that absorbs every defect it notices delivers something other than the work the epic scoped, and the criteria it was measured against stop describing it.

- **A standalone issue with no home is a decision postponed, not taken.**
  An orphan waits for a later pass to find it a place, and until then nothing says when it is fixed or what fixing it makes true.

- **Nothing records that the initiative is carrying debt.**
  An initiative whose epics are all closed reads as complete even when its delivery left known defects behind, because no row and no criterion names them.

## Proposal

- **One epic takes the whole of it.**
  Each item a unit defers becomes a row here, and the initiative stays open while any row is undelivered, so the debt is visible as outstanding work rather than as prose in a planning record.

- **Each row carries the criterion its fix makes true.**
  The statement is what the fix establishes, not the defect it removes, so the row is verified the same way any other row is.

- **The clear-up absorbs what it uncovers.**
  Debt a unit of this epic finds in resolving its own row becomes a further row here, so fixing one item cannot quietly widen another epic.

- **It is raised when the first item is deferred and grows as delivery proceeds.**
  Its rows are not planned ahead of the work that finds them.

content.title: [I00:E08] Validation Gate: Boundaries, Consistency and Diagnostics
content.body:
## Overview

The validation gate completes what candidate validation began. Region boundaries are proven safe, sources are rechecked for change, a generated document is refused as input, every failure produces a diagnostic a calling agent can act on, and validation follows the selection rather than the file. The tool is in use while this lands, so each row closes a way a bundle can be wrong that first use has already exposed or could.

## Problem

Provenance agreement is not the whole of correctness.

- **A boundary can swallow what follows it.**
  Two regions joined without safe separation can place later content inside an earlier code fence, HTML block, list or quote, which changes meaning without producing invalid Markdown.

- **A source can change mid-compilation.**
  Files are read during discovery and published after validation, so a source edited in between would be published from the bytes discovery captured rather than the bytes on disk.

- **Output read back as input compounds.**
  A published bundle already carries generated file headings and rewritten links, so bundling it again would rewrite generated structure as if it were source.

- **A failure the agent cannot explain is a failure twice.**
  Without a code, a location, the offending reference and the chain that reached it, a calling agent can report only that bundling failed.

- **A sound section is unreachable through an unsound document.**
  A check applied to a whole file refuses a run that selected one good section of it, so the defect of a region nobody asked for decides the outcome.

## Proposal

- **Boundaries are proven safe.**
  Emitted regions are separated and the result reparsed. A boundary that absorbs content into an unintended container fails with its declared code, naming the source regions and the conflicting boundary.

- **Sources are rechecked before publication.**
  Each source is compared against its captured content hash and canonical identity. A changed, removed or relocated source fails with a retry message.

- **A generated document is refused as input.**
  A source opening on a file heading is rejected, recognized by a document-level H1 whose text names a document under the root once a Markdown extension is appended, while a heading-like line inside code is not a heading and is not detection.

- **Diagnostics carry a stable shape.**
  Each carries an error code, the referring source location, the original reference, the resolved identity where one exists, the inclusion chain and a remedy where one can be stated accurately. A selected JSON format emits one object per line with no prose on that stream.

- **Validation follows the selection, not the file.**
  Link resolution, self-reference and syntax checks apply within the selected dependency closure. Parsing a whole file to index it does not make its unselected sections dependencies, so a broken or self-referential link in one of them does not fail a run that did not select it. If closure later includes that section, its links become subject to validation like any other.

- **An indexing failure is not a dependency.**
  A file-wide parsing-safety limit exceeded by an unselected construct fails as an inability to index that source safely, diagnosed as such rather than as a dependency on the construct that exceeded it.

| [W03](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/107) | Diagnostic content and the JSON format | AC4, AC5 | W01, W02 | | ✓ |
| [W04](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/110) | Validation scope and indexing failures | AC6, AC7, AC8 | W03 | | ✓ |
| [W05](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/106) | A definition the author spelled across two lines published inline | AC9 | [E05:W03](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/7) | | ✓ |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **AC2.** Each source's content hash and canonical path identity are captured at discovery and rechecked before anything publishes; a source that changed, disappeared or resolved elsewhere fails with a retry diagnostic and publishes nothing, as the consistency tests show. A fixture declares a static source tree, so the corpus states the capture and the recheck rather than a source changing mid-run.
- [x] **AC3.** A source opening on a file heading, whose text names a document under the root other than itself once a Markdown extension is appended, is rejected, while a document titled with its own name and a heading-like example in code are both bundled, as the generated-input fixtures show.

content.title: [I00:E09] Outline and Closure Completion: Ancestors, Grouping and the Measured Budget
content.body:
## Overview

Outline and closure completion finishes the structure a bundle presents and settles the output budget against a real measurement. Heading-only ancestors restore the outline a partial selection skipped, a depth beyond the sixth level fails rather than flattening, a grouping rule merges one part of the tree, the configured output budget is set from a bundling that was measured rather than assumed, and the design's usage examples name a tree the repository owns.

## Problem

A tool in use carries the structure its first users did without.

- **A selected child without its parents reads as a top-level topic.**
  Selecting a third-level section and emitting it alone discards the relationship that placed it under its parent.

- **A shift has a ceiling.**
  Markdown carries six heading levels, so a deep selection beneath a generated file heading can require a seventh, which has no heading spelling.

- **One document's sections are read beside another's.**
  Twenty documents in one closure carry an `Operations` section, and a bundle grouped by document puts each in a different place, so comparing them means reading twenty groups.

- **A budget nobody measured is a guess with a number on it.**
  An output limit set from an assumed figure either refuses bundlings that would have been fine or admits ones no caller can hold.

- **An example the repository cannot run is prose.**
  The design's usage examples name a tree that lives in another repository. No check reads them, no run executes them, and nothing notices when one stops being a valid invocation.

## Proposal

- **Ancestors appear as structural ancestors.**
  A selected section's unselected eligible ancestors are emitted as headings with escaped literal text and no body, siblings or other descendants. Structural ancestry is recorded separately from selected content and is not traversed for dependencies.

- **Overflow fails.**
  A bundling needing a heading beyond the sixth level fails rather than flattening, clamping or emitting heading-like text.

- **A group merges one part of the tree.**
  A group names a directory slug and a heading level, and every document beneath a directory of that slug is merged at that level, beneath one heading carrying the slug. A document no group names keeps its own group. A merged section carrying body text from more than one document splits into variants by document, since a procedure is its mode's own rather than a container of named items. A merged heading keeps its source text where that text occurs once; where several documents contribute one text, it is emitted once with each document's content beneath a variant heading naming that document, so the variants of a name sit together.

- **One budget is set by measurement.**
  The closure the proposal measured is bundled and its output size recorded against the configured budget, so the output limit rests on a real bundling rather than on an assumed figure.

- **The repository owns the tree its examples name.**
  A small example tree, taken from the closure of one real procedure and renamed, carries its references marked where the material is required and unmarked where it is cited, so it shows both halves of the rule in one place. The corpus bundles it, so an example that stops working fails a run rather than going quietly stale.

## Work Breakdown

| [W06](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/115) | Ancestor promotion over structural ancestors | AC9 | W02 | | ✓ |

## Acceptance Criteria

content.title: The Link Check Fails a Branch on a Third-Party Outage
content.body:
## Problem

`make links` resolves every remote reference the repository's documents carry and fails the run on any response it does not accept. A single request decides each reference, so a third-party host answering `503` fails the check, fails `make check`, and fails continuous integration on every branch at once — while the document, the reference and the resource it names are all correct.

Observed on 2026-10-20 during I00:E05:W01. Run [39382768119](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/actions/runs/39382768119) failed on:

```text
FAIL src/README.md: https://pypi.org/project/markdown-it-py/ — HTTP 503
FAIL src/README.md: https://pypi.org/project/types-jsonschema/ — HTTP 503
```

Neither URL is touched by that branch, and `https://pypi.org/project/markdown-it-py/` returned `503` to five consecutive direct requests from the host at the same time. The check reported a defect in the repository where the defect was in PyPI.

## Why it matters

A check that fails on something the repository cannot control teaches a reader to re-run it rather than to read it, which is the habit that lets a genuine broken reference through. It also blocks a merge the evidence supports: a session that must not merge on a failed run, and must not claim a run it did not get, has no move left but to wait on a third party.

## What a resolution looks like

The check distinguishes *this reference does not resolve* from *this host did not answer*. The shape is open:

- Retry a `5xx`, a timeout and a connection reset a bounded number of times with a delay, and fail only when the host is still unreachable.
- Report an unreachable host as its own verdict, separate from an unresolved reference, so the summary line says which of the two happened.
- Decide whether an unreachable host fails the check at all, or warns and passes, and state the decision where the check is described.

Whatever is chosen is stated in `checks/README.md`, because a check's verdict is part of the contract a reader is held to.

## Where it belongs

[#39 I00:E11](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/39) — the standalone checks and the gaps in them.

content.title: A Marked Image Reaches the Bundle With Its Mark
content.body:
## Problem

A marked image reaches the bundle with its mark intact.

`required` reads the links a source's selected content carries, and an image is not one of them, so `E_MARKED_RESOURCE` never fires on `![¬ the architecture](plan.png)`. A resource is emitted as the author wrote it and nothing rewrites it, so the mark survives into the published bundle.

Observed on 2026-10-20 during I00:E05:W02, against the rewrite that drops the mark from every link it reaches:

```text
$ prosiform --root source guide.md
This bundle was built for [guide](#guide); everything else is material it references.

# guide

The procedure follows ![¬ the architecture](plan.png), which is no
document the bundle carries.
```

A marked link naming the same file fails as it should; only the image form passes.

## Why it matters

D32 holds that the mark is authoring syntax and never reaches a reader, and D40 refuses a marked resource precisely so that invariant holds with no exception: *the mark is dropped by the rewrite and a resource is never rewritten, so the bundle would carry a mark, which the mark's own rule forbids.* The image form is the case that reasoning was written about, and it is the one case that still produces the bundle the decision ruled out.

It also leaves `I00:E04:AC17` claiming more than the build does. The criterion says a marked reference naming a resource fails with its declared error code; the marked-resource fixtures cover a scheme and a non-Markdown suffix, both written as links.

## What a resolution looks like

The classification reads image uses alongside link uses when it looks for the mark. An image's alternative content is the text its own token carries rather than the text following it, so the mark is read from a different place in the token stream, and the refusal and its diagnostic are the ones a marked link already takes.

`fixtures/rewriting/marking-an-image` declares the finished behaviour and carries the marker until this lands.

## Where it belongs

[#39 I00:E11](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/39) — the debt the prototype initiative's delivery defers. It blocks no criterion of the row that found it, and it warrants a work item of its own.

content.title: A Definition Whose Title Spans Two Lines Ends the Run in an Internal Error
content.body:
## Problem

A link-reference definition whose title the author wrote across two lines ends the run in an internal error.

The emission edits the lines one inline token occupies and writes no line break into them, because the group then slices those lines one for one against the parser's own maps. An inline target carrying a two-line title cannot be written under that rule, so the conversion refuses rather than publishing lines the group would mis-slice.

Observed on 2026-10-20 during I00:E05:W03:

```text
$ cat guide.md
# Guide

A [multiline][m] title.

[m]: m.md "A title
across lines"

$ prosiform --root source guide.md
E_UNEXPECTED_INTERNAL_ERROR: unexpected internal error: Unrewritable('the definition spelling '(m.md "A title\nacross lines")' spans two lines')
$ echo $?
4
```

## Why it matters

A two-line definition is ordinary CommonMark and the design names it: *Adversarial acceptance fixtures — Definition inventory* requires every selected definition occurrence to be removed, "multiline definitions" among them, and *Source-local reference interpretation* step 1 requires the use to be published inline. Exit status 4 is the status the contract reserves for a fault in the tool, so a source a reader would call unremarkable is reported as a defect in the build rather than bundled or refused with a code the contract names.

Before the conversion landed, the same source published a bundle carrying a dangling `[multiline][m]` whose definition had been removed, which stated nothing about the fault. The refusal is louder but is still not an outcome the contract declares.

## What a resolution looks like

The emission admits a region whose line count differs from its source's. That is the same capability a title spanning two lines needs and the one a use published inline across a line break needs, so the group slices against a map it rebuilds rather than against the parser's original one. Both the destination and the title are then carried as the author spelled them, across as many lines as they occupy.

## Where it belongs

[#59 I00:E08](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/59) — the validation gate, as `W05` and `AC9`. Its rows close the ways a bundle can be wrong that first use exposed, and this is one of them.

It blocks no criterion of the row that found it, so the deferred-debt epic was the other candidate. The severity places it here instead: a wrong bundle is still a bundle a caller can see and work around, while a run that publishes nothing and reports a fault in the tool leaves the caller nothing to act on and tells the author their correct document is not the problem. Recorded as `D45` in the planning record's decisions.

content.title: A Marked Link Inside Image Alternative Content Reaches the Bundle With Its Mark
content.body:
## Problem

A marked link written inside an image's alternative content reaches the bundle with its mark, and the document it names is not carried.

`required` reads the link events a source's selected content carries from the top level of each inline token. An image holds its alternative content in a run of its own, so a link written there is read by nothing: it is discovered as no dependency, assigned no destination, and rewritten by nothing.

Observed on 2026-10-20 during I00:E05:W03:

```text
$ cat guide.md
# Guide

A picture ![of the [¬ rules](rules.md) it names](plan.png).

$ prosiform --root source guide.md
W_RESOURCE_PORTABILITY: the bundle names at least one resource, ...
This bundle was built for [guide](#guide); everything else is material it references.

# guide

A picture ![of the [¬ rules](rules.md) it names](plan.png).
```

`rules.md` is never opened, the bundle carries no group for it, and the published link names a source path.

## Why it matters

D32 holds that the mark is authoring syntax and never reaches a reader. `I00:E05:AC3` states that every local Markdown link in selected content is rewritten to its target's destination, and `fixtures/rewriting/no-link-names-a-source-path` states that no published link names a source path. All three are false for this one position.

It also reports nothing: the run exits 0 and the mark the author wrote is published as text.

## What a resolution looks like

Dependency discovery reads an image's alternative content as the run of inline events it is, so a link written there is read where a link written beside the image is. The destination map, the occurrence count a budget is declared over, and the rewrite then reach it, and the emission already edits a span wherever it sits, nested or not.

## Where it belongs

[#39 I00:E11](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/39) — the debt the prototype initiative's delivery defers. It blocks no criterion of the row that found it, and it warrants a work item of its own.

content.title: Validation Scoped to Selected Content
content.body:
## Overview

Validation reads the content a run selected. A defect in a region the run did not select does not fail that run, so a fragment reference to a sound section bundles even where the rest of its document would be refused.

## Problem

A bundling refuses raw HTML, and a construct recognized as an unsupported dependency or section-naming extension, in *selected content*. The contract scopes both to selection, and its validation-scope fixtures state that an unselected sibling must not fail a narrow run.

- **Selection narrows nothing today.**
  A fragment reference reads the whole document it names, because section extraction does not exist. Selected content is therefore the entire source, and every refusal is evaluated over all of it.

- **A sound section is unreachable through an unsound document.**
  A reference naming one section fails when any other part of that document carries raw HTML or a recognized unsupported construct, although the bundle would carry none of it. The caller is refused content that is correct, for a defect in content it did not ask for.

- **The divergence is invisible while extraction is absent.**
  No fixture can state the narrow case until a fragment selects less than a document, so nothing fails today and nothing records that the scope is wrong.

## Proposal

- **A refusal is evaluated over selected content alone.**
  Once a fragment selects a region, the checks that refuse raw HTML and recognized unsupported constructs read that region and the structural ancestors emitted with it, not the document around them.

- **The whole-document case is unchanged.**
  A reference naming a document selects all of it, so a defect anywhere in that document still fails the run. The narrowing applies where the selection is narrow.

- **The boundary is the selection, not the file.**
  A document contributing two selected regions is checked over both and over nothing between them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** A fragment reference to a sound section of a document whose unselected content carries raw HTML or a recognized unsupported construct bundles successfully, while a whole-document reference to that same document fails, as the validation-scope fixtures show.

## References

- **R1.** [I00:E02:W02 validation record](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/tree/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-10-19-4-i00-e02-w02-profile-configuration-and-source) — where the divergence was found and recorded as a stated boundary: the row that introduced both refusals could not scope them, because selection did not exist.
- **R2.** [I00:E02 Walking Skeleton](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/4) — the epic whose AC7 and AC9 declare the two refusals this issue scopes.

content.title: Initiative Gates and Implied Edges: Eight Dependency Problems the Unreadable Cells Masked
content.body:
## Overview

With the cross-epic cells readable again, the dependency check reports eight problems against I00 that were masked while it could parse nothing. Six are initiative gates that the task graph does not support; two are cross-epic edges another edge in the same cell already implies. None changes what the build does, and all eight fail the check, so the plan cannot be run clean until they are answered.

## Problem

- **Six initiative gates disagree with the task graph.**
  `deps.py` derives a whole-epic prerequisite as one where every row of the other epic is a prerequisite of every row of this one, and reports an initiative cell naming anything else as overbroad.

  ```
  initiative E08: overbroad whole-epic dependency E06; retain specific task dependencies
  initiative E08: Depends on should be E05, not E06
  initiative E09: overbroad whole-epic dependency E03, E04; retain specific task dependencies
  initiative E09: Depends on should be empty, not E03, E04
  initiative E10: overbroad whole-epic dependency E08; retain specific task dependencies
  initiative E10: Depends on should be E06, not E08
  ```

  E08's cell names E06, but E08:W05 depends only on E05:W03 and consumes nothing from E06, so E06 is not a prerequisite of the whole epic. E05 is, because E05:W03 and E05:W04 share a pull request and the joined unit carries the rest of that epic's chain.

- **The cell is not inert, so emptying it is a behaviour change.**
  `board.py`'s `met` reads the initiative row's Depends on to gate the epic, and an empty cell is satisfied by definition. Clearing E09's cell would have released E09 before E03 and E04 closed. The gate the check wants removed is the gate the queue enforces, so each of the six is a decision about when an epic may start, not a formatting fix.

- **Two cross-epic edges are already implied.**

  ```
  E02:W06: E01:W02 is already implied by E02:W04
  E02:W08: E02:W04 is already implied by E02:W06
  ```

  Both are in a closed epic and neither changes any gate, since the implying edge carries the same reach.

- **D44 is the reason the initiative cells look as they do, and it is contrary to the skill's model.**
  The decision holds that a cross-epic dependency gates on the epic and the initiative row states the gate. The work-planner's position is the opposite: a task row names the rows it consumes and the initiative gate is derived from them, recorded upstream as [m2ux/workflow-server#1292](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/issues/1292) and being applied to other plans as [#1463](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/issues/1463). D44 has already been corrected once, for a spelling neither tool could read; this is the part of it that remains.

## Proposal

- **Decide each of the six against the work it gates, not against the check.**
  For E08, E09 and E10, read what the epic's rows consume and set the initiative cell to the epics the task graph supports, or record why the plan gates more coarsely than the graph.

- **Settle D44 against the skill's model.**
  Either retire the epic-grain rule and let the initiative gates be derived, or record the divergence and the reason the plan keeps a coarser gate, so a later reader is not told twice that the cells are wrong.

- **Drop the two implied edges, or state them as documentation.**
  E02 is closed and its reach is unchanged either way.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** The dependency check reports no problem against I00, as its run over the initiative and all twelve epic bodies shows.
- [ ] **AC2.** Each initiative gate that differs from the one the task graph derives is recorded in the planning record with why, as that record shows.
- [ ] **AC3.** D44 states one rule for a cross-epic dependency that both the dependency check and the board queue read without a problem, as a run of each shows.

## References

- **R1.** [Planning record](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/tree/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-10-17-prosiform-v1) — D44 holds the epic-grain rule, D52 the Joins correction made alongside this finding.
- **R2.** [m2ux/workflow-server#1466](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/issues/1466) — the skill-side defects this investigation found: a cell the checks cannot read is held as an unmet dependency rather than a malformed one, and the joins advisory rewards filling the column.

content.title: Branch Protection: Enabled When the Repository Becomes Public
content.body:
## Overview

Branch protection is enabled on this repository when it is made public, which is when the platform first offers it. Until then the delivery procedure is the only thing holding the branch shape, and that is a deliberate position rather than an oversight.

## Problem

- **The platform refuses protection while the repository is private.**
  A protection request answers with an upgrade notice, so `main` accepts a direct push, an unreviewed self-merge, and a force-push over a branch another writer holds.

- **The exposure grows with the writer count.**
  One session following the procedure is safe by construction. Work dispatched to separate sessions that raise and merge their own pull requests is not, and the first sign of a writer that does not follow the procedure is a surprising merge rather than a blocked push.

- **A condition is forgotten at the moment it is met.**
  Going public is a decision about disclosure. Nothing about it prompts a decision about branches, so the trigger passes unremarked unless something is waiting on it.

## Proposal

- **Enable protection on `main` when the repository becomes public.**
  Required pull requests before merge, no force-push, no branch deletion. All three become available at no cost at that moment.

- **Leave the long-lived branches matching the delivery model.**
  `main`, `engineering` and `workspace` are long-lived. Epic bases and task branches are created and deleted by the delivery procedure, so protection covers the long-lived set and leaves the rest alone.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** `main` requires a pull request before merge, refuses a force-push and refuses deletion, as the branch protection settings show.
- [ ] **AC2.** Creating and deleting an epic base and a task branch still succeeds under those settings, as a delivery run shows.

## References

- **R1.** [D30](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/blob/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-10-17-prosiform-v1/decisions.md) — the decision recording why discipline is convention until this issue is actionable.

content.title: [I00:E10:W04] Installation Claims No Fixture Can Reach
content.body:
## Overview

The conformance report lists the installation claims no fixture can reach, with the reason each one is unreachable, so the limits of what the corpus proves about installation are read from the report rather than from a planning record.

## Problem

The installation smoke run holds the entry point to being one: it builds the wheel, installs it into a throwaway environment, and invokes the command by name from a directory unrelated to the repository. Three claims about installation sit outside what that run can observe, and all three currently live only in a planning record.

- **Another platform.**
  The run observes this host and the `ubuntu-latest` runner. A Windows script wrapper and its path resolution are a different mechanism, and nothing records that the claim is unobserved.

- **A machine that never held the repository.**
  The repository exists on disk during the run and is merely unreachable by path, working directory and environment. A check that lives inside the repository cannot remove it, so the strongest form of the claim is unreachable from here.

- **The documented `pip install ./prototype` route.**
  The run installs a built wheel, which is what an environment receives either way, but the command line the README gives a reader is not the one executed.

None of the three is a corpus fixture: the corpus runs a build named by `PROSIFORM_BUILD`, and an installation is not a thing a fixture can name. A limit held only in a planning record is a limit nothing re-reads, so the three read as covered to anyone looking at the corpus.

## Proposal

- **The declared-surface listing carries installation claims alongside exit statuses.**
  AC5 already requires each exit status no fixture can reach to be listed as unfixturable with its reason. An installation claim no fixture can reach is the same kind of thing one layer up, and it belongs in the same listing rather than in a second place.

- **Each of the three is listed with the reason it is unreachable.**
  Another platform, a machine that never held the repository, and the documented `pip install ./prototype` route, each naming what would have to change for it to become observable.

- **A claim that becomes observable leaves the list.**
  Two of the three may never be fixable from inside the repository; the third becomes observable the day the smoke run executes the documented command line. The listing is generated from the corpus and the checks, so a claim stops being listed when something observes it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** The three installation claims the smoke run cannot observe are listed as unfixturable with the reason each one is unreachable, as the conformance report's declared-surface listing shows.

## References

- **R1.** [#61](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/61) — the installation smoke run these claims sit outside, and the three properties it does observe.
- **R2.** [I00:E07:W01 planning record](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/tree/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-10-19-19-i00-e07-w01-installation-and-stable-entry) — where the three are recorded today, with what each one would take to observe.

content.title: The Unexpected-Internal-Error Outcome Is Observed by Nothing
content.body:
## Overview

Exit status 4 and `E_UNEXPECTED_INTERNAL_ERROR` are declared by the contract and carried by the command's generic handler, and nothing observes either one.

## Problem

- **No instrument reaches the handler.**
  No corpus fixture declares the status, and no unit case raises anything the handler catches. The clause `Exit status and JSON diagnostics` states the outcome; the catalogue carries the code; the command carries the handler. Between them there is no observation.

- **The cases that looked like coverage were watching something else.**
  Three command-line cases touched status 4. Each named a fragment reference the build could not carry out, so each observed the section-selection stub standing in front of the handler rather than the handler itself. I00:E03:W02 delivered real selection, the stub went, and those cases went with it. They were never the handler's subject.

- **A declared outcome no instrument reaches is a claim, not a contract.**
  A build that returned the wrong status, the wrong severity or no diagnostic at all for an unexpected error would pass every check the repository runs.

## Proposal

- **Observe the handler directly.**
  A unit case makes the command raise an error the contract does not name, and asserts the status, the severity and the code the run reports on standard error, in both the text and the JSON diagnostic format.

- **A corpus fixture cannot do it.**
  An unexpected internal error is not a property of a source tree, so no declaration of sources, invocation and expected result can provoke one. The instrument is a unit case, and the catalogue entry stays exactly what the design declares.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** A command whose execution raises an error the contract does not name returns exit status 4 and emits one error diagnostic carrying `E_UNEXPECTED_INTERNAL_ERROR`, in both the text and the JSON format, as the unit cases show.

## References

- **R1.** [I00:E03:W02](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/72) — the delivery that removed the selection stub and, with it, the three cases that appeared to cover this outcome.

content.title: A Parser Resource Limit Suppressing a Reference Lookup Is Detected by Nothing
content.body:
## Overview

`E_PARSER_REFERENCE_LIMIT` is declared by the contract and by the fixture catalogue, and nothing in the build raises it.

## Problem

- **The detection does not exist.**
  The code appears in `src/prosiform/limits.py` only inside a docstring, distinguishing it from `E_RESOURCE_LIMIT`. No module defines it as a constant, no call site passes it, and no corpus fixture or unit case expects it.

- **The contract states a gate the build does not meet.**
  The design names it under *Mandatory parser viability gates*: detect when an internal parser resource limit prevents a reference lookup and fail, naming the first affected source span where one is available, and do not read a successfully exhausted budget with no later suppressed lookup as evidence that a reference was omitted.

- **A declared code nothing can raise is a claim, not a contract.**
  A reference the parser silently declined to resolve is a dependency the bundle omits without saying so, which is the failure mode the gate exists to close. Nothing in the repository would notice.

## Proposal

- **Observe the parser's suppression and fail on it.**
  Where the parser declines a reference lookup against an internal resource limit, the run fails with `E_PARSER_REFERENCE_LIMIT`, naming the first affected source span where the parser reports one, and carrying the fields a diagnostic about a reference carries.

- **Distinguish exhaustion from omission.**
  A budget consumed on its last valid reference, with no later lookup suppressed, is a successful run. A fixture states that case alongside the failing one, so the gate cannot be met by failing whenever the budget is spent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** A source whose reference expansion is suppressed by an internal parser resource limit fails with `E_PARSER_REFERENCE_LIMIT`, naming the first affected source span where one is available, as the parser-exhaustion fixtures show.
- [ ] **AC2.** A run that consumes the expansion budget on its last valid reference, with no later lookup suppressed, succeeds and claims no omitted reference, as the parser-exhaustion fixtures show.

## References

- **R1.** [I00:E08:W03](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/pull/107) — the review that found it: every declared code run and the fields it carries recorded, two of twenty-seven reachable by nothing.
- **R2.** [Design, Mandatory parser viability gates](https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/blob/engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-10-17-prosiform-v1/design.md) — the clause the code is declared under.
